summary: Yu counts ℓ-adic local systems of rank n on a curve over F_q that are fixed by Frobenius, through Drinfeld's method and the Arthur–Lafforgue trace formula, and relates the count to stable Higgs bundles and to geometrically indecomposable bundles through Mellit's polynomial A_{g,n}; for degree coprime to n it does not depend on the degree. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-seven findings are recorded. Lemma 6.3.2(b) is false for non-diagonalizable matrices (E16), Corollaries 4.2.6 and 6.1.2 need added hypotheses (E4, E15), and the rest are misprints or proof points. Not formalised. After the review (REV-PAPER-YU-23) there are 179 items (11 library, 25 planned, 143 missing) and 56 source issues; the most substantive are that Lemme A.2 is false when gcd(e, n) > 1, so Yu's own proof of Théorème 1.4 covers only e prime to n (the general case is Mellit's theorem), that the top-weight assertion of Théorème 1.1(1) is never proved (it is true), and that (5.3.2) pairs each root with the wrong Rankin–Selberg factor; Théorèmes 1.1–1.3 are otherwise unaffected.

items.name: Smooth proper curve and constant-field extensions
items.statement: X_1 is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over the finite field F_q; F is an algebraic closure of F_q; X_k = X_1 ⊗_{F_q} F_{q^k} for k ≥ 1 and X = X_1 ⊗_{F_q} F. F_X: X → X is the F-linear endomorphism deduced by extension of scalars from the F_q-endomorphism of X_1 which is the identity on the underlying topological space and f ↦ f^q on O_{X_1}. Fix a prime ℓ ∤ q and an algebraic closure Q̄_ℓ of Q_ℓ. Ranks are positive integers and degrees are integers.

items.name: Frobenius-fixed descent up to inertial twist
items.statement: An irreducible geometric rank-n representation extends to W(X1) iff its class is F_X-fixed. Any two extensions differ by an inertial character, giving a bijection between fixed classes and inertial classes of representations with irreducible geometric restriction.

uses.how: Input to Local-system count equals the absolute cuspidal count.
Input to Frobenius orbit inversion.

items.proofOutline: Choose an intertwiner from the representation to its Frobenius conjugate. It defines the action of a lift of Frobenius and hence of the semidirect Weil group. Schur's lemma makes two such choices scalar; scalar powers are precisely inertial twists. Check continuity on the geometric subgroup.
items.note: Review note: Statement matches. The 'F_X-fixed' form uses [DF13, Lemma 1.3] (conjugation by j(1) on classes of π_1(X,o)-representations equals F_X^* on E_n), which no item covers; proposed below as a new item and should be added to the dependencies.

items.name: Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer
items.statement: For irreducible rank-n sigma of W(X1), Fix(sigma) is cyclic of order d|n. Equivalently sigma is induced from a geometrically irreducible rank-n/d representation of W(Xd), whose d geometric Frobenius conjugates are pairwise nonisomorphic. The inducing class is unique up to that orbit. Fix=1 iff geometric restriction is irreducible.

items.proofOutline: First establish the semisimplicity/normalizer lemma used in Yu's argument (item123, still a source gate). Decompose geometric restriction into a transitive Frobenius orbit. items.statement: Fix unimodular Haar measures on Ξ_M, M_P(F), N_P(F), G(F), N_P(A), M_P(A) and G(A) for every parabolic P, such that the measures on Ξ_M, M_P(F), N_P(F) and G(F) are counting measures, vol(M_P(O)) = vol(G(O)) = 1, and vol(N_P(F)\N_P(A)) = 1. For a Levi M and a closed point x, H_{M,x} = C_c^∞(M(O_x)\M(F_x)/M(O_x)) with convolution for the local Haar measure giving M(O_x) volume 1, and unit 1_{M(O_x)}. H_M is the restricted tensor product of the H_{M,x} with respect to these units.

items.name: Spherical cuspidal automorphic forms
items.statement: Let θ be a character of Z_G(F)\Z_G(A)/Z_G(O). A_{G,θ,cusp} is the space of functions φ: G(F)\G(A) → C that are right K-invariant, satisfy φ(zg) = θ(z)φ(g) for all z ∈ Z_G(A) and g ∈ G(A), and satisfy ∫_{N_P(F)\N_P(A)} φ(ng) dn = 0 for all g ∈ G(A) and every proper standard parabolic P ⊊ G (E1). Right convolution makes it an H_G-module. A simple H_G-submodule of A_{G,θ,cusp}, for some θ, is an everywhere-unramified irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A). A_n(X_1) denotes the set of these.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §2.3.1 pp9–10, corrected E1

items.name: Spherical multiplicity one and the full representation distinction
items.statement: The fixed-central-character cuspidal spherical H_G-module is semisimple with multiplicity one, and each irreducible spherical H_G-module is one-dimensional. This does not say that the irreducible smooth G(A)-representation generated by it is one-dimensional.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §2.3.1, p. 10 (semisimplicity [Lau97, Thm 9.2.14]; multiplicity one [Sh74, Thm 5.5]); Remarque 1 after Définition 2.3.4, p. 11 (dimension one, by Flath and Satake)

items.name: Moeglin–Waldspurger classification
items.statement: (Moeglin–Waldspurger, [MW89, Théorème p. 606].) Let Π be a discrete everywhere-unramified automorphic representation of G_n(A). There are d | n, the standard parabolic P with M_P = G_d × ⋯ × G_d (ν = n/d factors), and an everywhere-unramified cuspidal representation π of G_d(A) such that, with |g| = q^{deg det g} and π̃ = π|·|^{(ν−1)/2} ⊗ π|·|^{(ν−3)/2} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ π|·|^{−(ν−1)/2}, Π ≅ π̃ as H_G-modules via t_P at every place. The pair (π, ν) is unique. Conversely, for every everywhere-unramified cuspidal π of G_d(A) and every ν ≥ 1, π̃ viewed as an H_G-module via t_P is isomorphic to the H_G-module of a discrete everywhere-unramified representation of G_{νd}(A), denoted π ⊠ ν.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §2.3.4, p. 12, Théorème 2.3.6 (the theorem is on p. 12 only)

items.proofOutline: Import the residual-spectrum classification. Normalize each cuspidal segment symmetrically, take the spherical Langlands quotient, and use uniqueness of cuspidal support to distinguish its length and cuspidal input. The original MW89 proof remains unread.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: Yu's statement (Théorème 2.3.6) identifies Π with π̃ = π|·|^{(ν−1)/2} ⊗ … ⊗ π|·|^{−(ν−1)/2} as an H_G-module via the constant-term homomorphism t_P: H_{G,x} → H_{M_P,x} (defined on p. 12). It is not stated as the 'spherical Langlands quotient of normalized induction'. That reformulation needs the Satake isomorphism and unramified principal-series theory, which the paper does not state. The converse is also a Hecke-module statement, with no central normalisation condition. Review note: AS.4 plans discrete, cuspidal and residual subspaces in general, not the Moeglin–Waldspurger classification of the GL_n residual spectrum. ET.7a plans the 'GL_m residual-spectrum/Speh classification … from the Moeglin–Waldspurger proofs', in the number-field unitary setting. The everywhere-unramified function-field version is not planned; 'planned: AS.4' overstates this. The t_P homomorphism it uses is proposed as a new item (FA.6). Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): status changed from planned to missing. AS.4 plans discrete, cuspidal and residual subspaces in general, not the Moeglin–Waldspurger classification of the GL_n residual spectrum; ET.7a plans that classification only in the number-field unitary setting. items.name: Krull–Schmidt for bundles
items.statement: Every vector bundle on X1 is a finite direct sum of indecomposable bundles, uniquely up to permutation and isomorphism. If rank and degree are coprime, an indecomposable bundle is geometrically indecomposable.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.2.2, p. 16, Lemme 3.2.1 (a lemma, not a theorem; proof by reference to [Sc16, Lemma 2.6])

items.proofOutline: Apply Krull–Schmidt to the Hom-finite category of bundles and split idempotents. For a geometrically decomposable indecomposable bundle, Frobenius permutes equal-rank equal-degree geometric summands transitively, forcing a common divisor of rank and degree.
items.note: Review note: Status missing is right. The uniqueness half can reuse the exchange argument of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/QuiverRepresentations Layer 2 (Krull–Schmidt, planned for finite-length modules and transported to categorical biproducts). Bundles are not finite-length objects, however: 'indecomposable ⇒ End local' must come from finite-dimensionality of End(E) over F_q (Atiyah), not from Fitting's lemma. The coprime geometric-indecomposability half is separate.

items.name: Shifted Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits
items.statement: If every Ti−Ti+1≥max(0,2g−2), the T-Harder–Narasimhan filtration is split. A nonsplit extension gives by Serre duality a nonzero map against the canonical twist, whose image/coimage slope inequalities contradict the gap.

items.proofOutline: Suppose the extreme HN extension does not split. Serre duality gives a nonzero map in the opposite direction with canonical twist. Pass to its image, saturation and coimage; the shifted-slope inequalities contradict deg omega=2g−2. Induct on the number of HN pieces. Ch15's full lemma proof was read.
items.note: Review note: Checked against Ch15 Lemme 4.2.1 (author p. 18). The hypothesis there is T_i − T_{i+1} ≥ max(0, 2g_C − 2), and the proof splits the last HN step by Serre duality and coimage/image slope bounds, with induction implicit. This matches the item.

items.name: Large-chamber isocline criterion
items.statement: For d(T)≥max(0,2g−2), a bundle with ordered isocline decomposition E_i is T-semistable iff Gamma_I((deg E_i),T)=1. Interpolate fundamental-weight inequalities with the corrected type-A convex identity; arbitrary subbundle ranks need this interpolation.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.1, p. 19, Proposition 3.3.4 (statement); proof §3.3.2, pp. 20–21 (E3)

items.proofOutline: Use the split HN filtration to reduce to sums of isocline summands. The lattice indicator checks the fundamental-weight inequalities at the block endpoints; the corrected three-index convex identity interpolates all intermediate ranks. Treat equality on walls explicitly.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The corrected identity (b−l)ϖ_a + (l−a)ϖ_b − (b−a)ϖ_l = −(b−l)Σ_{a<t<l}(t−a)α_t − (l−a)Σ_{l≤t<b}(b−t)α_t holds: the α_j-coefficient of ϖ_i is min(i,j)(n−max(i,j))/n, which is piecewise linear in i with a kink of −1 at i = j, and the interpolation defect of such a function is −(b−l)(j−a) for a<j<l and −(l−a)(b−j) for l≤j<b. For a<t<b we have α_t(H) = 0 and α_t(T) ≥ 0, which gives (b−a)ϖ_l(H−T) ≤ (b−l)ϖ_a(H−T) + (l−a)ϖ_b(H−T) ≤ 0, i.e. (3.3.8). The split HN step (Ch15 Lemme 4.2.1 plus Krull–Schmidt) then contradicts (3.3.9). The outline is complete.

items.name: Coprime scalar-nilpotent vanishing and the Fourier comparison
items.statement: (Chaudouard, D = 0.) Let gcd(n,e) = 1. (a) [Ch15, Thm 6.2.1] For monic p ∈ F_q[X] of degree n, the T = 0 value J̃_{p,e} of the Lie-algebra quasi-polynomial vanishes unless p = (X−α)^n with α ∈ F_q, in which case J̃_{p,e} = J̃_{nilp,e}. (b) [Ch15, Cor 5.2.3] For every T and e, Σ_p J̃^T_{p,e} = J^{T,e}_0 = q^{n²(1−g)} J^{T,e}_K, with K a canonical divisor. (c) [Ch15, Cor 5.2.2] Since deg K = 2g−2, J^{0,e}_K is the mass Σ 1/|Aut| of the groupoid of semistable Higgs bundles (E, θ: E → E ⊗ ω) of rank n and degree e over F_q. Hence J_e = (q−1)J̃_{nilp,e} = ((q−1)/q) Σ_p J̃_{p,e} = ((q−1)/q) q^{−n²(g−1)} mass(Higgs^{ss}_{n,e}(X_1)(F_q)).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Appendix B, p. 79; [Ch15, Théorème 6.2.1, Corollaires 5.2.2–5.2.3]

uses.how: Input to Higgs count and geometrically indecomposable bundles.

items.proofOutline: For the scalar-nilpotent support, follow Ch15 Thm6.2.1's reduction through characteristic-polynomial factors and the degree coprimality obstruction; its downstream lemmas remain to be read. For Fourier comparison apply Poisson summation to the two kernels. Ch15 Thm5.2.1 and its corollaries were read through their proofs.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The Ch15 hypothesis is attached to the wrong divisor. Ch15 Cor 5.2.2 says that for deg D' ≥ 2g−2 the trace J^{e}_{D'} itself (not J_{K−D'}) is the mass of semistable D'-twisted Hitchin pairs. Yu applies Cor 5.2.3 with D = 0, J_0 = q^{n²(1−g)} J_K, and then Cor 5.2.2 with D' = K (deg K = 2g−2). 'For deg D ≥ 2g−2 the latter trace is the semistable Higgs mass' is therefore wrong as written.

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Two independent checks. (i) Mellit, arXiv:1707.04214v1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2, reads H_g = −(1−q)(1−z) Log Ω_g. (ii) The T^1 coefficient of Log Ω_g is the one-box term Π_i (z−z_i)(1−q z_i^{−1}) / ((z−1)(1−q)), so the prefactor (1−q)(1−z) gives H_{g,1} = Π_i (z−z_i)(1−q/z_i), and at z = 1 this is |Pic^0|. The printed (1−g) would give a non-polynomial H_{g,1}, and zero for g = 1. The Ω_g formula in the item matches the TeX exactly.

items.name: Universal bundle polynomial from Mellit
items.statement: (Mellit [Me17, Thm 1.1] with Schiffmann [Sc16].) Let g ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, and define H_{g,n} by Σ_{n≥1} H_{g,n}T^n = −(1−q)(1−z) Log Ω_g. Then H_{g,n} is a Laurent polynomial in q, z, z_1, …, z_g (in Q[q^{±1}, z^{±1}, z_1^{±1}, …, z_g^{±1}] in Yu's notation). A_{g,n}(q, z_1, …, z_g) := H_{g,n}(q, 1, z_1, …, z_g) lies in Z[q, z_1^{±1}, …, z_g^{±1}] and depends only on g and n. For every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X_1 of genus g over F_q and every e ∈ Z, A_{g,n}(q, σ_1, …, σ_g), with σ_iσ_{i+g} = q, is the number of isomorphism classes of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles of rank n and degree e on X_1. For (e, n) = 1 it equals P_n^e(X_1). Every monomial q^m z_1^{a_1}⋯z_g^{a_g} of A_{g,n} satisfies m + Σ_i min(a_i, 0) ≥ 0.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.2.3, p. 17, Théorème 3.2.5 (second and third assertions) and the recollection of Mellit's formula; [Me17, Theorem 1.1]

items.proofOutline: Use Mellit's plethystic identity, with the corrected (1−q) prefactor, and the regular z=1 specialization. Match its degree-independent indecomposable-bundle count to Yu's coprime application. Mellit's introduction was checked, but the proof of polynomiality and the admissible-cone transport remain source gates.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'H_{g,n} is Laurent integral' is ambiguous. Neither Yu nor Mellit states integer coefficients for H_{g,n}: Yu writes H_{g,n} ∈ Q[q^{±1}, z^{±1}, z_i^{±1}], and Mellit says 'Laurent polynomial in q, z and α_1,…,α_g'. The integrality is for A_{g,n} ∈ Z[q, z_i^{±1}] (Schiffmann). The item should also say that A_{g,n} depends only on g and n, and that the evaluation is at σ_1,…,σ_g with σ_iσ_{i+g} = q. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The proof outline uses the corrected (1−q) prefactor, which Mellit's Theorem 1.1 confirms, and Mellit states the specialisation for all d, which matches 'covers all e'. The cone statement is proved correctly by Yu's (1+qR(q))^{−1} argument: fix the z-exponent and take the lowest q-power.

items.name: Weyl permutations and fixed Levis
items.statement: Let M be a semi-standard Levi subgroup of G=GL_n and w in W_n (a permutation matrix). Put w(M)=wMw^{-1}; then w(a_M)=a_{w(M)} and w induces an isomorphism w: X_M^G -> X_{w(M)}^G, w(λ)(m)=λ(w^{-1}mw) for m in w(M)(A). If w(M)=M (so w permutes the blocks of M, necessarily among blocks of equal size), there is a smallest Levi subgroup L_w containing M and w; it is characterized by a_{L_w}=ker((w−id)|a_M), its blocks are the unions of the blocks of M along the cycles of the block permutation induced by w, and w acts trivially on X_{L_w}^G. For M ⊆ L, restriction of characters gives an inclusion X_L^G ⊆ X_M^G. Track the lattices a_{M,Z}, a_{L,Z} as well as the real spaces.

items.name: Arthur theta denominator and multiplicative families
items.statement: For a semi-standard Levi L, the chambers of a_L^G correspond to P(L) via P ↦ {H in a_L^G : α(H)>0 for all α in Δ_P}; P̄ denotes the opposite parabolic (Φ_P̄=−Φ_P), and P,Q in P(L) are adjacent when |Φ_P̄ ∩ Φ_Q|=1. For Q in P(M) and λ in X_M put θ_Q(λ)=∏_{α in Δ_Q}⟨λ,α^∨⟩ (the linear pairing of 4.1.6, so ⟨λ,α^∨⟩=λ_u−λ_v for α^∨=e_{M,u}−e_{M,v}); this differs from Arthur's θ_Q by a volume factor. Let Ω ⊆ X_M^G or X_M be a domain. A family (c_P)_{P in P(M)} of holomorphic functions on Ω is a (G,M)-family if c_P(λ)=c_{P'}(λ) for every adjacent pair P,P' and every λ in Ω with λ^{α^∨}=1, where α is the unique root in Φ_P ∩ Φ_{P̄'}. For such a family c_M(λ)=Σ_{Q in P(M)} c_Q(λ)θ_Q(λ)^{-1} is meromorphic on Ω. A domain around a noncentral translate must be specified when one is used.

items.name: Regularized family value and descent
items.statement: (a) Let (c_Q)_{Q in P(M)} be meromorphic on X_M^G (or X_M) and a (G,M)-family on a neighbourhood of λ0 in X_M^G (or X_M). Then c_M(λ)=Σ_Q c_Q(λ)θ_Q(λ)^{-1} is regular at λ0. (b) For a (G,M)-family near 1 put c_M=lim_{λ→1}c_M(λ). For L in L(M), R in P(L) and Q in P^L(M), c^R_Q(λ)=c_{QN_R}(λ) (QN_R the unique element of P(M) contained in R with QN_R ∩ L=Q) is an (L,M)-family near 1, with value c^R_M=lim_{λ→1}Σ_{Q in P^L(M)} c^R_Q(λ)θ^L_Q(λ)^{-1}, θ^L_Q(λ)=∏_{α in Δ^L_Q}⟨λ,α^∨⟩. (c) For Q in P(L) and λ in X_L^G, c_Q(λ):=c_P(λ) for any P in P(M) with P ⊆ Q is independent of P and defines a (G,L)-family near 1.

items.proofOutline: Subtract adjacent chamber values; the wall-compatibility condition cancels the corresponding simple-root denominator. Iterating over walls makes the total sum regular. Restrict characters along nested Levis to prove the two descent constructions. Arthur's original regularization proof is still an imported leaf. Freshly read Laf97 VI.2 Lemma7 pp303–304: fix a root wall, pair permutations in which its two labels are adjacent, and use their equal wall values to divide their difference by the wall equation. Other terms have no pole there. Repeating over all root walls removes the product denominator; intersections do not introduce a new pole. Corollary10 applies this to the full family before the contour reaches the unitary locus.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: Théorème 4.2.2 (Arthur 1981, Lemma 6.2) gives regularity of c_M at any point λ0 of X_M^G (or X_M) near which the family is a (G,M)-family, not only at 1. The item states it only near 1, but item 055 (Lemme 4.2.8) needs it at a translate μ0 ('la limite existe car (c_Q) est une (G,M)-famille sur un voisinage de μ0', p. 28). Review note: Arthur's additive originals (1981 Lemma 6.2) are in the AS.6 corpus (AutomorphicSpectralTheory:AS.6, '1981 §6 ... supply the (G,M)-family arguments'); the multiplicative X_M^G version is a source addition via route 3, as recorded.

items.proofOutline: Linearize one root factor at a time and use regularization to discard terms of degree below dim(a_M^G). The surviving squarefree terms correspond exactly to root bases; their lattice determinants fix the normalization. Yu's induction supplies the multiplicative-family version.
items.note: Review note: Statement checked, including a rank-one test (M=T in GL_2: c_M=c'_β(1)+c'_{−β}(1)). Its proof uses Arthur's basis identity [Ar82, pp. 1319–1320], which no item covers (coverage entry below), and contains the E5 misprint and a notational slip (ξ in X_P^G; new issue below).

items.name: Root-coordinate Haar integral
items.statement: For a root basis F and continuous functions on S1, the map Im X_M^G→(S1)^F has finite central kernel and pushes probability Haar measure to probability Haar measure. Consequently the product integral factors into the one-variable contour integrals with dz/(2πi).

items.proofOutline: The exponent homomorphism of compact tori associated to a root basis is surjective with finite kernel. Pushforward of probability Haar measure is probability Haar measure. Fubini then turns the product into independent circle integrals.
items.note: Review note: Faithful. The kernel of u_F is X_G^G≅μ_n because a set of type-A coroots e_u−e_v forming a basis of a_M^G (a spanning tree) generates the full lattice {x in Z^r : Σx=0}. The paper never normalizes dλ; the lemma forces probability Haar (take f_β(z)=z^{-1}); see the new issue below. The item's probability-Haar reading is the right one.

items.name: Argument-principle integral of a family
items.statement: Assume each c_beta is meromorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and nonzero and finite on S1. For the ratio root-product family, its integrated regularized value is Σ_F∏_{beta∈F}(N(c_beta)−P(c_beta)), counting multiplicities in |z|<1. Rational L-ratios satisfy the needed extension assumption when boundary singularities are absent.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Corollary4.2.6 p27, corrected E4

items.proofOutline: Apply item52 to the translated ratio family. Integrate each logarithmic derivative via item53, then use the argument principle on the disk. Meromorphic continuation to the disk and absence of boundary zeros/poles are essential, not consequences of meromorphicity on C* alone.
items.note: Review note: Corrected statement (E4) checked: with c_β meromorphic near the closed disc and nonzero and finite on S^1, the regularized value is Σ_F∏_{β in F} c'_β(λ^{β^∨})λ^{β^∨}/c_β(λ^{β^∨}), and Lemma 4.2.5 plus the argument principle give the stated count. Théorème 4.2.4 requires c_β meromorphic on C^×, but its proof is local at 1, so it applies to z ↦ c_β(az)/c_β(a).

items.name: Ambient independence and central-translation vanishing
items.statement: (a) [Lemme 4.2.7] If c_Q(λ)=∏_{β in Φ_Q} c_β(λ^{β^∨}) as in Théorème 4.2.4, then for every L in L(M) the value c^R_M is independent of R in P(L) (write c^L_M): c^R_Q=∏_{β in Φ(Z_M,N_Q)}c_β(λ^{β^∨})·∏_{β in Φ(Z_M,N_R)}c_β(λ^{β^∨}), and the second factor tends to 1. (b) [Lemme 4.2.8] Let μ0 in X_M^G and let (c_Q) be a (G,M)-family on a domain containing μ0^Z such that c^R_M is independent of R in P(L) for every L in L(M) and c_Q(λμ0)=c_Q(λ) wherever c_Q is defined. Then lim_{λ→1}Σ_{Q in P(M)} θ_Q(λμ0)^{-1}c_Q(λμ0)=0 unless μ0 in X_G^G, and for μ0 in X_G^G it equals μ_{01}^{−dim a_M^G} c_M, where μ_{01} is the (common) first coordinate of μ0.

items.name: Degree-filtered lattice cone series
items.statement: Let M be standard, Q in P(M) and s in W_n/W^Q with sQs^{-1} standard. Let φ_Q be the indicator of {H in a_{s(M)} : for all α in Δ_Q, ϖ_{s(α)}(H)≤0 if α(κ)>0 and ϖ_{s(α)}(H)>0 if α(κ)<0}, where ϖ_{s(α)} in Δ̂_{sQs^{-1}} is dual to s(α)^∨, and let ε(Q)=#{α in Δ_Q : α(κ)<0}. Then 1̂_Q(λ) on X_M^G is the analytic continuation of (−1)^{ε(Q)}Σ_{H in a_{M,Z}/X_*(Z_G)} φ_Q(s(H))λ^{−H}, which converges where |λ^{α^∨}|<1 for all α in Φ(Z_M,G) with α(κ)>0 (a region meeting every component of X_M^G). For semi-standard L and Q in P(L), 1̂_Q(λ):=1̂_{wQw^{-1}}(w(λ)), where w in W_n/W^{Q_L} is the unique element with wQ_Lw^{-1} standard. For ζ a primitive n-th root of unity, η=ζ^{deg det} in X_G^G and e in Z, 1̂^e_Q(λ)=n^{-1}Σ_{k=1}^n ζ^{ek}1̂_Q(λη^k); it is the part of the series with Σ_iH_i≡e (mod n), and 1̂_Q=Σ_{e=0}^{n−1}1̂^e_Q.

items.name: Corrected Arthur–Lafforgue spectral expression
items.statement: For G=GL_n over F_q(X), n>0, the everywhere-unramified trace at T=0 is J_eta=Σ_[(P,pi)] |stab(P,pi)|⁻¹ Σ_[(w,tau)∈stab(P,pi)] ∫_(lambda∈A) D⁻¹ Σ_[(a,c)∈mu_w⁻¹(tau)] F_eta(lambda,a,c) d lambda. Here A=Im X_L^G, B=Im X_M^L, L=L_w, mu_w(a,c)=a*c/w⁻¹(c), D=|w||X_L^L|, and F_eta is the exact ordered regularized trace151 with h_Q(v)=hat1_Q(v eta⁻¹). Haar on A has total mass one, including all components. The finite fibre is equivalently a∈A,b∈B0,tau=a*b,c∈B,δ_w(c)=b. Replacing h_Q by hat1_Q^e gives J_e for every e∈Z. No good-representative hypothesis is required for this spectral identity. Its proof and scalar specialization require the coherent normalization and analytic prerequisites retained in S2.

items.proofOutline: Start with Laf97 VI.2 Lemma9/Corollary10, not its unexpanded Theorem11. Yu (5.2.10) shifts the contour variable by eta⁻¹. Decompose the parameter in A*B using probability-Haar pushforward142, and replace (w,tau) by its inverse (w⁻¹,w(tau)⁻¹) to obtain (5.2.11). After the regularized Q-sum is smooth, apply149 to its character coefficient to evaluate on mu_w⁻¹(tau). This gives exactly151, with D⁻¹. Item152 recovers each degree. Source-to-operator identification still imports Langlands unitarity, functional equations and gluing; S2 does not claim those original proofs or the rho dictionary fully closed.

For S,R in P(M): M_{R|S}(λ)φ_S=n_{R|S}(π,λ)φ_R with n_{R|S}(π,λ)=∏_{β in Φ(Z_M,G), β in Φ_S ∩ Φ_{R̄}} n_β(π,λ^{−β^∨}) (equivalently ∏_{α in Φ_R ∩ Φ_S̄} n_{−α}(π,λ^{α^∨})), n_β as in (5.1.1); for L ⊇ M and Q,Q' in P(L) group the factors over β restricting to α in Φ(Z_L,G). In particular M(w,λ)φ_P=n_π(w,λ)φ_P for (w,1) in stab(P,π). The factor q^{(1−g)n_in_j} comes from vol(N(F)\N(A))=1 versus local vol(N(O_v))=1 (vol(F\A)=q^{g−1} for the product measure). Prove the local Gindikin–Karpelevich factors, the restricted Euler product and the global Haar factor separately.

items.proofOutline: Compute each local intertwiner on the normalized spherical vector. Multiply the unramified factors and include the global unipotent Haar volume q^((1−g)ni nj). Adjacent-parabolic composition gives the full product; source images fix the normalization in E8/E12. The global additive-volume factor is unchanged by the present continuation. The rho ambiguity now has the explicit153 transport contract; no scalar formula is asserted independent of a change of normalization without that proof.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'the product of the appropriate root normalizers' hides a real error in the source. Yu's (5.3.2) attaches n_α(π,λ^{α^∨}) (the factor built from L(Π_j×Π_i^∨)) to each α in Φ_R ∩ Φ_S̄. The Gindikin–Karpelevich computation gives n_{−α}(π,λ^{α^∨}), i.e. L(Π_i×Π_j^∨) for β=−α=e_i−e_j in Φ_S ∩ Φ_{R̄}. This agrees with Yu's own 'en particulier' formula and with (5.1.2). The basis must also be fixed as φ_R=ρ_Rφ_π (E8). Review note: See the new issue on (5.3.2). It has no effect on Proposition 5.1.1 (item 067): for good pairs, (w,1) in stab inverts only roots between equal factors, the n_{S|P} ratio is 1 at central λ_L, and in (c) the exchange L(Π_i×Π_j^∨) ↔ L(Π_j×Π_i^∨)=conj L(Π_i×Π_j^∨)(z̄) preserves the zero and pole counts in |z|<1. E12 is confirmed.

items.name: Cuspidal Rankin–Selberg degrees and poles
items.statement: Let π1, π2 be unitary everywhere-unramified cuspidal automorphic representations of G_{n1}(A) and G_{n2}(A); write L(π1×π2^∨, z) = P(z)/Q(z) with P, Q coprime and P(0) = Q(0) = 1. (i) If n1 ≠ n2, or n1 = n2 and π1 ≇ π2⊗λ for every λ ∈ X_{G_{n2}}, then Q = 1 and deg P = (2g−2)n1n2. (ii) If π1 = π2 and d = |Fix(π1)|, then Q(z) = (1−z^d)(1−(qz)^d), deg P = (2g−2)n1² + 2d and ε(π1×π1^∨) = q^{(g−1)n1²}. (iii) If π1 ≅ π2⊗λ with λ ∈ X_{G_{n2}}, then λ = α^{deg∘det} with |α| = 1 (both representations are unitary) and L(π1×π2^∨, z) = L(π2×π2^∨, α'z) for some α' with |α'| = 1 (α' = α^{±1} according to the degree sign convention), so (ii) holds after z ↦ α'z.

items.proofOutline: Use Langlands to express the Rankin–Selberg factor as the tensor local-system cohomology determinant. Schur's lemma and the geometric orbit decomposition determine H0/H2; Euler characteristic determines deg H1. Purity separates the numerator and denominator root radii and prevents cancellation.

items.name: Residual Rankin–Selberg product and zero–pole index
items.statement: Let Π_k = π_k ⊠ ν_k (k = 1, 2) be unitary everywhere-unramified discrete automorphic representations of G_{n_kν_k}(A), π_k cuspidal of rank n_k. Then L(Π1×Π2^∨, z) = ∏_{i=1}^{ν1}∏_{j=1}^{ν2} L(π1×π2^∨, q^{(ν1+ν2)/2+1−i−j} z). Let N(f), P(f) be the numbers of zeros and poles of f in |z| < 1, counted with multiplicity. Then N−P of L(Π1×Π2^∨, z)/L(Π1×Π2^∨, q^{−1}z) equals min(ν1,ν2)(2g−2)n1n2 if Π1 and Π2 are not inertially equivalent. It equals min(ν1,ν2)(2g−2)n1n2 + |Fix(π1)| if Π1 ∼ Π2, i.e. ν1 = ν2 and π1 ∼ π2, in particular if Π1 = Π2. For a good representative, Π_i ≠ Π_j implies Π_i ≁ Π_j, so the paper's two-case form (ν1 ≥ ν2; '≁' and '=') suffices there.

items.proofOutline: Expand both residual segments into cuspidal twists and multiply their L-factors. Shift the variable, telescope adjacent segment factors and count zeros/poles using item68. Only good representatives justify the stated equal-or-disjoint dichotomy; arbitrary unequal inertial twists require a separate formula.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: (1) 'An extra |Fix(π1)| precisely when Π1 = Π2' and 'the inertially-equivalent but unequal case needs an explicit twist convention' are wrong for arbitrary unitary pairs. If Π1 ∼ Π2 (ν1 = ν2 and π1 ≅ π2⊗λ, λ necessarily unitary), then L(π1×π2^∨, z) = L(π2×π2^∨, α'z) with |α'| = 1, all zero and pole radii are unchanged, and N−P = ν2(2g−2)n1n2 + |Fix(π1)|. So the extra term occurs exactly when Π1 ∼ Π2, and no convention is needed (E15). (2) n1 and n2 (the ranks of the cuspidal π1, π2, not of Π1, Π2) are not defined in the item. (3) The count holds for either order with min(ν1,ν2), which is the form Theorem 6.4.1 uses. (4) The item bundles Lemma 6.1.3 with Corollary 6.1.2, and a split is proposed under coverage. items.note: Review note: missing is right (route 12). Proof outline: the paper proves Proposition 6.2.4 only for e = −1 and defers the other e to Theorem A.4, whose argument has the flaw E26. items.name: Rank-one cofactor identities
items.statement: If A1=0, kappa(A)=det(A+1vᵀ)/(nΣv) for Σv≠0. If also 1ᵀA=0, all principal cofactors agree and kappa(A)=det(A+uvᵀ)/((Σu)(Σv)) when both sums are nonzero. Derive these by determinant multilinearity/adjugates, including rank below n−1.

items.proofOutline: Expand a determinant after a rank-one update, using cofactors and A1=0. With both left and right kernels containing 1, the adjugate is a scalar multiple of 11^t, including the zero adjugate in smaller rank. Extract the coefficient of t in det(A+tI).

items.name: Correct eigenvalue formula for kappa
items.statement: For singular complex A, kappa(A) is the product of the remaining n−1 eigenvalues divided by n after removing one zero eigenvalue, counted algebraically; it is zero if zero has algebraic multiplicity≥2. The product of nonzero eigenvalues is valid only when zero is simple. Rank n−1 alone is insufficient.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma6.3.2(b), corrected E16
items.proofOutline: Factor the characteristic polynomial over C with algebraic multiplicities. The coefficient of its linear term is the product after deleting one zero root; it vanishes when zero has multiplicity at least two. The nilpotent 2-by-2 example disproves the stronger printed claim.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. det(A+tI) = ∏(t+μ_i) over the eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity, so [t]det(A+tI) = e_{n−1}(μ). This is the product of the remaining n−1 eigenvalues after deleting one zero root, and it is 0 when 0 has algebraic multiplicity ≥ 2 (in particular when rank < n−1). The factorisation argument is complete. Python (sympy): A = [[0,1],[0,0]] gives κ = 0 = the average principal cofactor, against the printed 1/2; B = [[0,1,0],[0,0,0],[0,0,5]] (rank 2) gives κ = 0, against the printed 5/3. The paper's only use, (6.4.6), has a simple zero eigenvalue.

items.name: Spanning trees and type-A root bases
items.statement: The edges of the complete graph on the ordered Levi blocks correspond to roots in −Phi_Q. A set of r−1 edges is a tree iff the corresponding roots form a basis of a_L^{G,*}; cycles give linear dependencies and paths span all differences. Hence the root-basis weighted sum equals kappa of its Laplacian.

items.proofOutline: Orient edges by the chosen positive-root order. A graph cycle gives a signed sum of root vectors equal to zero. In a tree each difference of vertices is the sum along its unique path, so its r−1 edge roots form a basis. Apply the matrix-tree theorem.

items.name: Representation-ring interpretation
items.statement: Restriction to the diagonal torus identifies R(GSp_2g) with Z[t±1,z_i±1]^W. Highest-weight theory gives polynomial generators t±1 and ∧^k V−t∧^(k−2)V, 1≤k≤g. The subring generated by constituents of tensor powers of V is R_g, generated by t and those fundamental expressions.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Remark7.1.1 p64
items.proofOutline: Import the existing classical-group highest-weight and character theory, then construct its rational GSp and central-similitude extension. Restriction to a split maximal torus yields the Weyl-invariant Laurent ring. Triangularity of fundamental exterior characters proves the generator statement. The rational descent and tensor-generated subring are new obligations, not applications of finite-group character injectivity.
items.note: Split representation rings exist (item141), but rational algebraic GSp representations and their Weyl-character identification need a Part II of the existing classical-group roadmap. Review note: Statement checked. The dominant weights of GSp_2g are z^u t^m with u_1 ≥ … ≥ u_g ≥ 0 and m ∈ Z, so R(GSp_2g) = Z[t^{±1}][V_{ω_1},…,V_{ω_g}], where V_{ω_k} = ∧^kV − t∧^{k−2}V. Every weight z^{u'}t^{m'} of an irreducible with highest weight z^u t^m and m ≥ 0 satisfies m' + Σ min(u'_i,0) = m + (|u| − Σ|u'_i|)/2 ≥ 0, and this gives the tensor-generated description. The remark only explains; nothing in the proof of Théorème 1.1 uses it. Partial planned suppliers are tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups Layer 4 (Weyl characters of Sp) and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/LieHighestWeight Layer 6. The GSp Grothendieck ring and its tensor-generated subring remain missing.

items.name: Density and uniqueness of universal polynomials
items.statement: The Frobenius Weil tuples of genus-g smooth proper geometrically connected curves are Zariski dense in the relevant torus modulo W, in the form of Schiffmann AppendixB used by Yu. Consequently two invariant Laurent polynomials agreeing on all such curves agree identically. This is not ordinary density of arbitrary algebraic numbers.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.1 p65; Sc16 AppendixB

uses.how: Input to Rank induction and Euler-product factors.
Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.proofOutline: Import the density result for curve Frobenius tuples with exactly the fixed genus and coefficient variables used here. A Laurent polynomial vanishing on that dense subset is zero. The original Schiffmann AppendixB density proof is still to be read and decomposed.
items.note: Review note: Correct as a citation of [Sc16, App. B], which was not re-read (paywalled). The paper's own inputs give a simpler route. Fix one curve from item 121, so that q, σ_1,…,σ_g are multiplicatively independent. If a Laurent polynomial P satisfies P(q^k,σ^k) = 0 for all k ≥ 1, then distinct monomials have distinct bases q^mσ^u, and Σ c_{m,u}(q^mσ^u)^k = 0 for all k forces every c_{m,u} = 0 (Vandermonde, item 140). Théorème 1.1(1) requires the identity for all k ≥ 1, so this proves uniqueness without Schiffmann's density theorem. The dependency 100 → Sc16 can therefore be replaced by 121 + 140.

items.name: Independent-monomial coefficient formula
items.statement: Fix a partition λ = (i^{a_i}) ⊢ n, where only the parts with a_i ≥ 1 matter, and fix l | n. Put g̃^λ_(i,l)(z^l) = Π_(s=1)^(n−1) Π_(j=1)^(l_s+m_s) Σ_(k≥0) (−1)^k binom(ε_(j,s)(2g−2)sS_i(λ)/l, k)(X^i_(j,s))^(lk) z^(skl), with independent variables X^i_(j,s). Here ε_(j,s) = −1 for the m_s denominator monomials α_(j,s) of η_(s,X_l) and ε_(j,s) = +1 for its l_s numerator monomials β_(j,s). In (1/(n(2g−2)Σ_i a_i)) Σ_(l|n) μ(l) Π_i [z^{a_i}] g̃^λ_(i,l)(z^l), the monomial Π_(i,j,s)(X^i_(j,s))^{k^i_(j,s)}, with k^i_(j,s) ∈ N, has coefficient 0 unless Σ_(j,s) s k^i_(j,s) = a_i for every i. In that case gcd(k) | n, and the coefficient is (1/(n(2g−2)Σ_i a_i)) Σ_(l | gcd(k^i_(j,s))) μ(l) (−1)^{Σ_(i,j,s) k^i_(j,s)/l} Π_(i,j,s) binom(ε_(j,s)(2g−2)sS_i(λ)/l, k^i_(j,s)/l).

items.proofOutline: Factor each rank-smaller counting polynomial into independent monomial placeholders in the Euler product. Expand each factor by generalized binomial coefficients. Coefficient matching forces the stated weighted k sums; then collect the terms with a common divisor l and the expansion signs.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The item leaves the sign implicit, and the paper prints it wrongly. Lemme 7.2.1 (p. 66) has (−1)^{Σ_(j,s) s k^i_(j,s)/l}, with the weights s included and the index i unbound. Its proof displays no sign at all and writes k_(j,s) ∈ N*. The binomial expansion gives (−1)^{Σ_(i,j,s) k^i_(j,s)/l}, which is the sign Théorème 7.2.3 uses (new issue). For example, with a single i, a_1 = 3, the monomial X_(j,2)X_(j',1) and l = 1, the true sign is +1 and the printed sign is −1.

items.name: Divisibility of generalized binomial coefficients
items.statement: For nonzero integer N and positive M, the integer N/gcd(N,M) divides binom(N,M), including negative upper entries. Use M binom(N,M)=N binom(N−1,M−1) and coprimality after dividing the gcd.

uses.how: Input to Primitive exponent valuation bound.
Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.proofOutline: Use M choose(N,M)=N choose(N−1,M−1), valid also for negative integral N. Divide N and M by their gcd; coprimality forces N/gcd(N,M) to divide the binomial coefficient.
items.note: Review note: Checked. The divisibility holds for every N with 0 < |N| ≤ 40 and 1 ≤ M ≤ 29, including negative upper entries. The proof via M·binom(N,M) = N·binom(N−1,M−1) is correct.

items.name: p-free factorial
items.statement: For a prime p and integer N≥0 define f_p(N)=∏_{1≤i≤N,p∤i}i=N!/[p^floor(N/p) floor(N/p)!]. It is a p-adic unit, including f_p(0)=1. Negative arguments are not admitted.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.2 p71; LZ19 equation10

uses.how: Input to Luo–Zhu p-free factorial congruence.

items.name: Luo–Zhu p-free factorial congruence
items.statement: For p odd and alpha≥1, or p=2 and alpha≥2, f_p(p^alpha N)≡f_p(p^alpha)^N mod p^(2alpha) for N≥0. Also f_2(2N)≡(−1)^floor(N/2) mod4. Pair i and p^alpha−i in the unit-residue sum and induct on N.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.2 p71; Luo–Zhu2019 Lemma3.1, proof read

uses.how: Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.proofOutline: Factor f_p(p^alpha N) into p^alpha-sized blocks of units. Expand each block to first order modulo p^(2alpha); pair inverse residues i and p^alpha−i so the linear correction vanishes. Induct on N. For p=2, alpha=1 separately count odd factors modulo four.
items.note: Review note: Checked numerically: 192 cases with p ∈ {3,5,7}, α ≤ 3 and p = 2, α ∈ {2,3}, N ≤ 11, plus f_2(2N) mod 4 for N < 60, all agree. The congruence fails for p = 2, α = 1 (for example N = 2), so that exclusion is necessary. The bibliography key is [LZ16], although the article appeared in Commun. Number Theory Phys. 13 (2019), 81–100.

items.name: Primitive exponent valuation bound
items.statement: Let p be prime and m ≥ 1. Let a_1,…,a_m ≥ 1 be integers, let J_i and K_i ⊂ N_(≥1) be finite sets, and let k^i_(j,s) ∈ N satisfy Σ_(j∈J_i,s∈K_i) s k^i_(j,s) = a_i. Let ν_1,…,ν_m ∈ Z, S_i = Σ_(j<i) ν_j a_j + ν_i Σ_(j≥i) a_j, and χ ∈ Z∖{0}, and assume every S_i ≠ 0. If p ∤ gcd_(i,j,s)(k^i_(j,s)), then v_p(Π_(i,j,s) χsS_i/gcd(χsS_i, k^i_(j,s))) ≥ v_p(χ S_m Σ_j a_j). Factors with k^i_(j,s) = 0 equal 1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.2.4 pp67–70; restricted nonzero range

uses.how: Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.proofOutline: Choose a nonzero k with minimal p-adic valuation and order the blocks by nu. Compare prefix and suffix partial sums of the weighted k constraints. At least one of the chi s S_i factors contributes each valuation needed for chi S_m sum(a); item103 turns those factors into binomial divisibility.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The item is restricted without need. Yu's Lemme 7.2.4 uses the data of Théorème 7.2.3: arbitrary integers ν_i, with no positivity or ordering. Its proof needs only S_i ≠ 0 and χ ≠ 0, and never uses that χ is even. Review note: Proof re-checked step by step: per-index cases 1) and 2), the prefix inequality (7.2.8), the suffix inequality (7.2.10) and the case i_0 = i_1. Random tests all satisfy the bound: 171,117 cases with ν_i ∈ [−5,6] and even χ, and 171,200 cases with odd or negative χ.

items.name: Möbius-binomial integrality
items.statement: Let m ≥ 1 and a_1,…,a_m ≥ 1. Let J_i and K_i ⊂ N be finite sets and k^i_(j,s) ∈ N with Σ_(j,s) s k^i_(j,s) = a_i. Let ν_1,…,ν_m ∈ Z, S_i = Σ_(j<i) ν_j a_j + ν_i Σ_(j≥i) a_j, ε_(i,j,s) ∈ {±1}, and χ ∈ 2N. Then Σ_(l | gcd(k^i_(j,s))) μ(l)(−1)^{Σ_(i,j,s) k^i_(j,s)/l} Π_(i,j,s) binom(ε_(i,j,s)χsS_i/l, k^i_(j,s)/l) is divisible by χ S_m Σ_j a_j; if χ S_m = 0 the sum is 0. Reduction to Yu's proof: (a) If χ = 0, or some S_i = 0, or some s = 0 carries k > 0, then every product contains a factor binom(0, k/l) with k > 0 and vanishes; a_i ≥ 1 guarantees some k^i_(j,s) > 0. (b) If S_i < 0, replace (ε_(i,j,s), S_i) by (−ε_(i,j,s), −S_i); this changes neither the binomials nor the valuations. (c) If ε = +1 and 0 ≤ χsS_i < k, the products at levels l and lp both vanish. In the remaining case, χsS_i > 0 and χsS_i ≥ k whenever ε = +1, and Yu's argument applies: items 104–106, the p-factorial binomial identities of p. 71, and the parity computation for p = 2 with v_2(gcd) = 1. In the application (item 108), ν_1 < … < ν_m are the distinct part sizes of λ, S_m = n and χ = 2g − 2.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem7.2.3 pp67–73

uses.how: Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.proofOutline: For each prime split the Mobius sum into l and lp pairs. Rewrite binomial quotients using p-free factorials; item105 gives the extra 2v_p(gcd k) cancellation beyond item106. Treat the p=2 valuation-one case by the explicit parity identity. This proves only the positive application range recorded, with broader printed edge cases left in S5.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The item is restricted without need. The edge cases its note leaves open (zero or negative ν_i, χ = 0) are resolved, and the theorem holds as Yu states it. Yu's proof, however, only treats χsS_i > 0 (new gap issue). Review note: Checked: 20,000 random instances all satisfy the divisibility (m ≤ 3, ν_i ∈ [−4,5], χ ∈ {0,2,4,6}, random ε). It fails for χ = 1 in 226 of 3,000 instances, so evenness is essential. The binomial identities of p. 71 were checked for p ≤ 5 and n < 8 with no failures, and the sign cancellations in both cases of the proof were re-derived. The S5 gate 'zero/negative edge cases' can be closed with the reduction above.

items.name: Integral universal local-system polynomial
items.statement: For all integers g ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1 there is a unique P_(g,n) ∈ R_g = Z[z_1,…,z_g, t/z_1,…,t/z_g]^{S_g⋉(S_2)^g} with the following property. For every finite field F_q, every smooth projective geometrically connected curve X_1/F_q of genus g, every prime ℓ ∤ q and every k ≥ 1, |(E_n^(ℓ))^{Fr_X^{*k}}| = P_(g,n)(q^k, σ_1^k,…,σ_g^k), where σ_1,…,σ_(2g) are the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^1, indexed so that σ_iσ_(i+g) = q.

uses.how: Input to Top weighted term of the counting polynomial.
Input to Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial.
Input to Low genus and low rank boundary counts.

items.proofOutline: Induct on n using the unique coefficient-one C_n term in item97 and the integral bundle polynomial. Introduce independent monomials for lower ranks and apply items102 and107 to every correction coefficient. The admissible exponent cone is closed under products and Adams powers. Density gives uniqueness.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The hypotheses are abbreviated. Théorème 1.1(1) quantifies over every prime ℓ ∤ q (the count does not depend on ℓ) and fixes the indexing σ_iσ_(i+g) = q. Review note: Checked end to end for small cases. A_(g,n) was computed exactly from Mellit's formula as recalled in §3.2.3, with the prefactor (q−1)(1−z); this reproduces A_(g,1) = J_g and so confirms E2. P_(g,n) was then solved from the recurrence of Théorème 1.2. For g = 2 (n ≤ 4) and g = 3 (n ≤ 3), P_(g,n) has integer coefficients, lies in the cone and is W-invariant.

items.name: Top weighted term of the counting polynomial
items.statement: Assign degree 2 to t and degree 1 to each z_i. For g≥2, P_g,n has unique top-weight term t^[(g−1)n²+1] with coefficient one; every other monomial has smaller weight. The leading bundle-polynomial term and strict rank-partition weight inequalities must be proved, not inferred from integrality alone.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem1.1(1) p3; §7.2 with Sc16 asymptotics
items.proofOutline: Use the leading term of the bundle polynomial from Schiffmann's asymptotics. For a nontrivial rank partition, strict quadratic rank inequalities make every recurrence correction lower weight. This isolates t^((g−1)n²+1); the asymptotic source proof remains open.
items.note: Review note: The paper states this on p. 3 but never proves it: nothing in §7 treats the top term (new gap issue). A proof route has two steps. (i) A_(g,n) has the unique top-weight term t^{(g−1)n²+1}, with coefficient 1 (proposed new item). (ii) By induction, every correction term of (7.2.2) is a rational multiple of a product Π_j C_(s_j)(X_(k_j)) with all s_j < n and Σ s_jk_j ≤ n. Since Σ k_js_j² ≤ (n−1)Σ k_js_j and Σ k_j ≤ Σ k_js_j, its weight is 2Σ k_j((g−1)s_j²+1) ≤ 2((g−1)(n−1)n + n), which is less than 2((g−1)n²+1) for g ≥ 2. Checked: the top term of P_(g,n) is exactly t^{(g−1)n²+1} for g = 2 (n ≤ 4) and g = 3 (n ≤ 3).

items.name: Jacobian factor of the bundle polynomial
items.statement: For g≥1,n≥1, A_g,n=I_g,n J_g with J_g=∏(1−z_i)(1−t/z_i), and I_g,n is integral and has the same admissible monomial cone. Each nonempty Young diagram contains the corner factor; Adams operations preserve divisibility by J, then Gauss's lemma and the cone filtration prove integral admissible division.

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.
Input to Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial.

items.proofOutline: Every nonempty Young diagram supplies the corner numerator J. Show divisibility persists through Adams operations and the plethystic logarithm, first rationally. J has a primitive extreme Laurent coefficient, so Gauss's lemma gives an integral quotient. Use the cone filtration to retain admissibility; its Laurent constant coefficient is not one.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. The extraction replaces the printed 'constant term 1' (E23) by primitivity, and this is correct: the coefficient of z_1⋯z_g in J_g is (−1)^g. Two points for the formaliser. (a) Apply Gauss's lemma first over the UFD Q[q^{±1},z^{±1}], where J_g = Π(z−z_i)(1−q/z_i) is also primitive, so that the quotient has no pole at z = 1 before specialising; the paper specialises without saying so. (b) The 'cone filtration' must use, for each S ⊆ {1,…,g}, the additive functional φ_S(t^m z^u) = m + Σ_(i∈S) u_i. Then ord_S is additive on products, ord_S(J_g) = 0, and m + Σ min(u_i,0) = min_S φ_S. The paper's single functional m + Σ min(u_i,0) is only superadditive, so its minimal-term argument does not exclude cancellation (new gap issue). Checked from Mellit's formula: I_(g,n) is integral, lies in the cone and is W-invariant for g ≤ 3 and n ≤ 3, and for g = 2, n = 4.

items.name: Euler specialization of the bundle quotient
items.statement: For g ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, I_(g,n)(1,1,…,1) = μ(n)n^{2g−3}. The proof imports four separate substantial inputs: purity of the coprime Higgs moduli, Schiffmann's point-count/Poincaré comparison, the nonabelian Hodge comparison with twisted character varieties, and Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas's PGL_n Euler characteristic. For g = 1, I_(1,n) = 1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof p74

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the local-system quotient.

items.proofOutline: Identify the compact-support Poincare specialization using Higgs purity and the count comparison. Pass to the twisted character variety by nonabelian Hodge theory, match the Jacobian/PGL quotient, and apply the HR08 Euler characteristic. Each geometric comparison is an unclosed original-source leaf.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: Missing hypothesis g ≥ 2. Lemme 7.3.1 is printed with no genus restriction. For g = 1, however, A_(1,n) = J_1 (Atiyah; also recomputed from Mellit's formula for n ≤ 3), so I_(1,n) = 1, while μ(n)n^{−1} is not even an integer when n ≥ 2 is squarefree. Review note: Checked from Mellit's formula: I(1,…,1) = −2, −3, 0 for g = 2, n = 2, 3, 4, and −8, −27 for g = 3, n = 2, 3. These agree with μ(n)n^{2g−3}. For g = 1 the value is 1 when n = 1, 2, 3.

items.name: Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1, P_g,n=Q_g,n J_g with Q_g,n∈R_g. The rational recurrence and induction first give divisibility over Q, then primitive-polynomial division gives integral coefficients; the cone argument keeps Q admissible. Thus #Pic^0(Xk)(F(q^k)) divides #E_n^(F_X^k).

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the local-system quotient.
Input to Low genus and low rank boundary counts.

items.proofOutline: Induct in the recurrence: all lower-rank C factors and the bundle term have J, and J of Adams-powered variables is divisible by J. Obtain rational divisibility, then use the primitive Laurent polynomial argument and cone filtration from item110.
items.note: Review note: Checked: J_g divides P_(g,n), and Q is integral, in the cone and W-invariant, for g = 2 (n ≤ 4) and g = 3 (n ≤ 3). On p. 74 the paper says only that Q_(g,n) exists 'par récurrence, le lemme précédent et le lemme de Gauss'. The cone property of Q needs the φ_S argument of item 110(b) (new gap issue). Integer divisibility follows because Q(q^k,σ^k) is rational and an algebraic integer.

items.name: Euler specialization of the local-system quotient
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1, Q_g,n(1,...,1)=Σ_{d|n}mu(d)mu(n/d)d^(2g−3). The linear part of the trace recurrence is Σ_{d|n}C_d(X1); after division by J and evaluation at one every nonlinear term vanishes. Apply Möbius inversion to item111.
items.proofOutline: Divide the trace recurrence by J and set all variables equal to one. Every term with two surviving counting factors vanishes; the linear terms are the divisor sum of the Q values. Substitute item111 and use Mobius inversion.
items.note: Review note: Derivation checked. The linear part of (7.2.1) is Σ_(d|n)Σ_(l|d)Σ_(s|d/l) μ(l)s²/d² C_s(X_(d/s)) = Σ_(d|n) C_d(X_1). The printed middle expression drops the factor s²/d², which equals 1 on the surviving terms (new misprint). The nonlinear terms are divisible by J_g², because J_g(t^k,z^k)/J_g(t,z) is a Laurent polynomial. Values checked: Q(1) = 1, −3, −4, 2 for g = 2, n = 1..4, and 1, −9, −28 for g = 3, n = 1..3.

items.name: Low genus and low rank boundary counts
items.statement: For n=1, Q_g,1=1 and P_g,1=J_g. For g=0 or1 and n≥2 there are no irreducible geometric rank-n local systems, so P=Q=0; this uses trivial or abelian geometric fundamental groups. The recurrence dividing by 2g−2 cannot be specialized to g=1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §1, p. 4, unnumbered Remarque after Théorème 1.1; §7.2.1, p. 65
items.proofOutline: For genus zero the geometric etale fundamental group is trivial; for genus one it is abelian, so characteristic-zero irreducibles have rank one. The rank-one formula is item40. These arguments handle g=1 independently of the singular recurrence denominator.
items.note: Review note: Statement checked. For g ∈ {0,1}, Théorème 1.1 does not define P_(g,n) or Q_(g,n), since it assumes g ≥ 2. The Remarque means the counting polynomials, which exist trivially in this case. Also A_(1,n) = J_1 for every n (item 111).

items.name: Degree floor-monomial family
items.statement: Set I_Q^e=H_Q^e+s^−1(0,1,...,1). The functions lambda↦lambda^I_Q^e form a (G,M)-family, and hat1_Q^e=(−1)^dim(a_M^G)lambda^I_Q^e/theta_Q. Adjacent-block compatibility follows from the floor identities on the wall.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), LemmaA.1 p75; Laf97 Lemma5(ii)p301
