items.note: Review note: Checked for every standard Levi of GL_n with n ≤ 7 and at most 4 blocks, every e ∈ [−n,2n) and every adjacent pair Q_s, Q_s'. In all 56,616 cases the difference I^e_(Q_s) − I^e_(Q_s') lies in Z(e_u − e_v) + Z(n_1,…,n_r), so the two monomials agree on the wall inside X_M^G. The item's sign (−1)^{dim a_M^G} correctly replaces the printed (−1)^{dim a_L^G} in (A.0.2) (new misprint).

items.name: Translated degree-cutoff vanishing
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and e ∈ Z with gcd(e,n) = 1. Let M be a standard Levi of GL_n and μ_0 ∈ X_M^G. Let (c_Q)_(Q∈P(M)) be a (G,M)-family on a domain containing μ_0^Z such that c_M^Q is independent of Q ∈ P(L) for each L ∈ L(M), and such that c_Q(λμ_0) = c_Q(λ). Then lim_(λ→1) Σ_(Q∈P(M)) 1̂^e_Q(λμ_0)c_Q(λμ_0) = 0 unless μ_0 ∈ X_G^G. Proof: d_Q(λ) = 1̂^e_Q(λμ_0)θ_Q(λ), multiplied by θ_Q as in E24, is a (G,M)-family by Lemme A.1 and the argument of Lemme 4.2.8. By Prop. 4.2.3 the limit equals Σ_L c_M^L d_L. If μ_0 ∉ X_L^G, then d_L = 0. If μ_0 ∈ X_L^G with L ≠ G, then d_L is a nonzero constant times Σ_(Q∈P(L)) 1̂^e_Q(μ_0) (the L-level functions), and this sum vanishes by the proposed coverage item because gcd(e,n) = 1. Finally d_G = 0 unless μ_0 is central. For gcd(e,n) > 1 the conclusion is false.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), LemmaA.2 pp75–76, E24

uses.how: Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.proofOutline: Use the product-family formula with the corrected d_Q=hat1_Q theta_Q. Partial-value independence makes all noncentral translated contributions vanish by the same missing-pole argument as item55.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: False as stated: Lemme A.2 needs gcd(e,n) = 1, and the item inherits the error (new issue). Counterexample: n = 2, M = T, c_Q ≡ 1, e = 0 and μ_0 = (i,−i) ∈ X_M^G, which is not central. Prop. 5.2.1 gives 1̂^0_B + 1̂^0_(B̄) = 1/(1−λ_1/λ_2) + 1/(1−λ_2/λ_1) ≡ 1, so the limit is 1. Likewise, for n = 10, M = GL_5×GL_5 and e = 2, the sum Σ_Q 1̂^2_Q is identically 1. Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: unsound. The corrected d_Q (E24) is right. But the outline's claim that partial-value independence makes every noncentral translated contribution vanish, 'by the same missing-pole argument as item 55', fails for gcd(e,n) > 1: the L-level sums Σ_(Q∈P(L)) 1̂^e_Q do not vanish when (n/gcd(m_j)) | e. With gcd(e,n) = 1 and the vanishing lemma added, the argument is sound. Numerical checks: with c ≡ 1 at random noncentral μ_0, the sum is 0 for every coprime e, and 1, −1 or a root of unity for several non-coprime e, over 12 Levis of GL_2 to GL_6. With random μ_0-periodic root-product families and μ_0 on walls of proper Levis, the limit is O(x) → 0 for coprime e; for non-coprime e it converges to stable nonzero values, for example −12.04 and 11.86 in GL_4 with e = 0 and e = 2. Downstream, item 119 and (5.3.6) of §5.3.3 hold only for coprime e.

items.name: Dependence of cutoff values only on degree order
items.statement: Under the same partial-value compatibility, lim_(mu→1)Σ_Qhat1_Q^e(mu)c_Q(mu) depends only on the order of e in Z/nZ. On a Levi with block sizes m_j, the top-degree floor-monomial contribution vanishes unless n|e m_j for every j; product descent gives the assertion.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), LemmaA.3 pp76–77

uses.how: Input to Spectral reduction to finite characters and root counts.
Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.proofOutline: Expand the floor-monomial exponential family at the identity. The top-degree coefficient survives exactly under the divisibilities n|e m_j; these depend only on gcd(e,n). Descend through all Levis using the product formula to obtain invariance for the full limit.
items.note: Review note: Checked. The proof's case split is complete: the fractional parts {e r^i_t/n} start and end at 0, so all ε^{t,e}_i vanish for one t iff they vanish for all t iff n | e m_j for every j. Numerically, with random root-product families, the limit agrees for e and e' of the same order (GL_3 with e = 1, 2; GL_4 with e = 1, 3).

items.name: Degree-order invariance of the finite character sum
items.statement: For c=gcd(l_j f_j), c|n and a=Σl_j(l_j−1)f_j/2, delta_e depends only on ord(e mod n). Since 2a=0 mod c, a is zero or the unique element of order two. Thus e+a=0 is detected solely by whether ord(e mod c) is respectively one or two, avoiding the false lcm-of-orders assertion.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), TheoremA.4 proof p78, E26

uses.how: Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.proofOutline: The shift a satisfies 2a=0 modulo c. In a cyclic group it is either zero or the unique element of order two; e+a=0 is therefore determined by whether e has order one or two, respectively. Combine with reduction from Z/nZ to Z/cZ. The printed general lcm identity is false.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. 2a = Σ(l_i−1)·l_i|Fix(π_i)| ≡ 0 mod c, so a ∈ {0, c/2}, and e + a ≡ 0 mod c iff ord(e mod c) = ord(a mod c) ∈ {1,2}. Since c | n (asserted on p. 78), ord(e mod c) is determined by ord(e mod n). This replaces the false lcm claim (E26).

items.name: Degree independence of the trace and isocline count
items.statement: For every n ≥ 1 and all e, e' prime to n: J_e = J_(e'), P_n^e(X_1) = P_n^(e')(X_1), and the number of geometrically indecomposable vector bundles of rank n and degree e on X_1 does not depend on e. This follows from items 116 (coprime case), 117, 118, 027 and 034. The general statement, that J_e and P_n^e depend only on the order of e in Z/nZ, is Théorème 1.4 as printed. For gcd(e,n) > 1 it must be imported from Mellit [Me17] or proved from a repaired Lemme A.2.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem1.4; TheoremA.4 andCorollaryA.5 pp77–78
items.proofOutline: In the spectral expansion use item117 for the degree cutoff and item118 for the finite character factor; Haar integration is translation-invariant. Thus the trace depends only on degree order. Item34 transfers this to isocline bundles and item27 gives the coprime indecomposable consequence.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The paper's argument in Appendix A proves this only for e and e' prime to n. The proof rests on (5.3.6), which §5.3.3 (p. 41) derives from Lemme A.2 'pour tout e ∈ Z', and Lemme A.2 is false when gcd(e,n) > 1 (item 116, new error issue). For gcd(e,n) > 1 the same-order statement (Théorème 1.4) is attributed to Mellit [Me17] and is not proved by Yu's argument. Review note: Only the coprime case feeds Théorèmes 1.1 and 1.2, since Prop. 5.1.1 assumes (e,n) = 1. The first nontrivial non-coprime instance is n = 10 with e = 2 versus e = 4: they are not related by e ↦ −e or e ↦ e + n, and Lemme A.2 fails there for M = GL_5×GL_5.

items.name: Valuation test for distinct exponential sums
items.statement: In a finite extension of Q_p (or a complete algebraically closed extension), take distinct nonzero gamma_i of positive valuation and nonzero integral c_i. Then some k≥1 has Σ c_i gamma_i^−k nonintegral. A Vandermonde system on r successive values bounds the valuations of c_i gamma_i^−k uniformly, contradicting their linear decay.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC unnumbered lemma p81

uses.how: Input to Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone.

items.proofOutline: Assume all negative power sums integral. Solve r consecutive sums by the Vandermonde inverse of the distinct gamma_i^(-1). Its finitely many coefficients give a lower bound independent of k on v(c_i gamma_i^(-k)), contradicting v(gamma_i)>0 as k grows.
items.note: Review note: Checked. The paper's proof, by successive differences and the remark that γ^{−k}a_k → 0 forces a_k → 0 when v(γ) ≥ 0, is correct, and so is the extraction's Vandermonde proof.

items.name: Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data
items.statement: For every prime p and genus g≥1 there exists a smooth proper geometrically connected ordinary curve over some F_(p^d) such that p^d,sigma_1,...,sigma_g are multiplicatively independent. For g=1 use Honda–Tate; for g≥2 use the nonempty ordinary locus, full geometric Sp monodromy, a density-one set of mod-l monodromy groups and Chavdarov's sieve with infinitely many auxiliary primes.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kow06,KS99,Kob75,Ch97

uses.how: Input to Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone.

items.proofOutline: For g=1 apply item137. For g≥2 restrict the universal family to its nonempty ordinary open, retain full geometric monodromy, use item135 to find a maximal-Weyl fibre, and apply item136. Original sources and the infinitely-many-primes adaptation remain S7.
items.note: Review note: Checked. Ordinarity makes each σ_i have valuation 0 or d, with exactly one of each pair of valuation d, which is condition (1). For g = 1, p and a root σ of X²+X+p are multiplicatively independent, because σ/σ̄ is not a root of unity for an ordinary curve.

items.name: Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone
items.statement: Fix a prime p. If P∈Z[t±1,z_i±1] takes integer values on every genus-g smooth proper geometrically connected curve over finite fields of characteristic p, for all choices of paired eigenvalues, every supported monomial t^m z^u satisfies m+Σmin(u_i,0)≥0. Choose the ordinary independent curve, orient the pairs according to negative exponents and apply item120 to its constant extensions.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), TheoremC.1 pp79–81, E27
items.proofOutline: Choose the ordinary independent tuple of item121 and orient each reciprocal pair so its valuation detects the negative exponents in a forbidden monomial. Multiplicative independence separates all evaluated monomials. Across constant extensions, item120 forces a nonintegral value, contradicting the hypothesis.
items.note: Review note: Checked, reading the hypothesis as holding for every choice of indexing. The proof re-indexes the pairs, so the hypothesis is needed for all choices (or P must be W-invariant). Only integrality at p, applied to all constant-field extensions, is used.

items.name: Normalizer semisimplicity input for the Weil representation argument
items.statement: Let σ: W(X_1,o) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) be an irreducible ℓ-adic representation, and let G_géom be the Zariski closure of σ(π_1(X,o)). G_géom is reductive, since σ|π_1(X,o) is semisimple by Clifford's argument, and it is normalised by γ = σ(j(1)). Then there exist u ∈ G_géom(Q̄_ℓ) and an integer d_0 ≥ 1 such that uγ^{d_0} commutes with every element of G_géom and with γ. Used for: if σ|W(X_{d_0},o) is irreducible, then uγ^{d_0} is a scalar, so every G_géom-stable subspace is W(X_{d_0},o)-stable and σ|π_1(X,o) is irreducible. The exact hypotheses must be read from [KW01, Théorème 3.3(2)] (gate S4). Weil II 1.3.9 (G_géom° semisimple for a pure twist) may be needed.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Proposition2.1.3 proof p7; KW01 Theorem3.3(2)

uses.how: Input to Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer.

items.proofOutline: Yu invokes KW01 Thm3.3(2) to control the normalizer and reduce irreducibility to a transitive semisimple geometric restriction. This checkpoint does not supply an exact source-checked theorem or a proof; S4 must replace this bounded input contract before completeness.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: The statement does not match what Yu uses. Yu needs the following (p. 7, attributed to Grothendieck via [KW01, Théorème 3.3(2)]): there are u ∈ G_géom(Q̄_ℓ) and d_0 ≥ 1 such that uσ(j(d_0)) commutes with G_géom and with σ(j(1)). He then applies Schur's lemma. The item speaks of 'the semisimple part of a suitable power … inside the group generated by G and scalar/central data', which is a different and vaguer assertion. Review note: statementStatus 'incomplete-source-contract' is right. The corrected statement records the exact contract Yu relies on.

items.name: Clifford–Mackey induction across constant extensions
items.statement: For the finite-index normal inclusion W(Xd)⊂W(X1), a geometrically irreducible representation with pairwise distinct d conjugates induces irreducibly, and restriction decomposes as their direct sum. Prove continuous finite-dimensional induction, Frobenius reciprocity and the conjugacy criterion on this finite quotient; generic finite-group carrier results alone do not supply the topology.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Proposition2.1.3 proof pp7–8

uses.how: Input to Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer.

items.proofOutline: Define induction using finitely many cosets of the normal geometric-constant-extension subgroup, preserving continuity. Compute the restricted representation as the sum of its conjugates. Frobenius reciprocity and pairwise inequivalence show that an endomorphism of the induced representation is scalar and yield the irreducibility criterion in the semisimple setting.

items.name: Serre duality for the shifted-slope argument
items.statement: For bundles U,V on a smooth projective curve, Ext1(U,V) is dual to Hom(V,U⊗omega). The actual image, saturated image, and coimage degree inequalities are needed to apply the slope bounds when the induced map is not a subbundle inclusion.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Ch15 Lemma4.2.1 proof; Yu§3.3.2

uses.how: Input to Shifted Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits.

items.proofOutline: Import coherent Serre duality on the smooth projective curve and use Ext1(U,V)=H1(U^vee tensor V). Pair with H0(V^vee tensor U tensor omega). The HN application must separately control the saturation and torsion quotient of a nonzero map.
items.note: Review note: SF.3 lists Serre duality among curve foundations. The form needed here, Ext^1(U,V) ≅ Hom(V, U⊗ω)^∨ for vector bundles, must be exported explicitly, not only for line bundles.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan existence with shifted slopes
items.statement: ([Ch15, Théorème 4.1.2].) Let E ≠ 0 be a vector bundle of rank n on X_1 and T ∈ R^n with T_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ T_n. There is a unique filtration by subbundles 0 = F_0 ⊊ F_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ F_r = E, with n_i = rk F_i, such that (1) F_{i+1}/F_i is (T_{n_i+1}, …, T_{n_{i+1}})-semistable for 0 ≤ i ≤ r−1, and (2) μ_T(F_1/F_0) > μ_T(F_2/F_1) > ⋯, where μ_T(F_{i+1}/F_i) = μ(F_{i+1}/F_i) − (T_{n_i+1}+⋯+T_{n_{i+1}})/(n_{i+1}−n_i). Then r = 1 if and only if E is T-semistable. If E is not T-semistable, then μ_T(F_1) > μ_T(E), since μ_T(E) is the rank-weighted average of the μ_T(F_{i+1}/F_i), so F_1 violates (3.3.5).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.2, p. 20 ('existence et unicité de la filtration de Harder-Narasimhan'); [Ch15, Théorème 4.1.2]

uses.how: Input to Shifted Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits.

items.proofOutline: Use boundedness of degrees of subbundles to choose a maximal shifted-slope subbundle, then a maximal rank among ties. Saturation and the sum/intersection inequalities give uniqueness; repeat on the quotient. The shifted version's exact Ch15 source proof remains to be read.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: 'T-semistable successive quotients' is imprecise. In Ch15 Thm 4.1.2 (author p. 17) the quotient F_{i+1}/F_i is (T_{n_i+1}, …, T_{n_{i+1}})-semistable, i.e. semistable for the block sub-vector of T, and the T-slopes μ_T(F_{i+1}/F_i) = μ(F_{i+1}/F_i) − (T_{n_i+1}+⋯+T_{n_{i+1}})/(n_{i+1}−n_i) decrease strictly. Yu also uses the consequence that F_1 violates (3.3.5) when E is not T-semistable.

items.name: Global Whittaker uniqueness and factorization
items.statement: A cuspidal GL_n automorphic representation is globally generic with multiplicity-one Whittaker functional for the chosen nontrivial additive character of A/F; its factorizable spherical vector has the restricted product of normalized local Whittaker functions. State the conductor and Haar choices rather than assuming an everywhere-conductor-zero global character.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §5.3.1 pp36–38; Shalika74,Flath79

uses.how: Input to Degree-zero nonvanishing of a spherical cusp form.
Input to Spherical Whittaker nonvanishing with conductor shift.

items.proofOutline: Import global Whittaker multiplicity one and local uniqueness; identify the global functional with the restricted tensor product of normalized local functionals on factorizable vectors. Conductor and Haar comparisons remain explicit, and originals Shalika/Flath were not read.
items.note: Review note: Faithful to the use in Lemme 5.3.3. Planned AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 is plausible ('global unfolding for cuspidal data'). The additive character with conductor n_v is a separate input (coverage entry below, planned FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.2).

items.name: Spherical Whittaker nonvanishing with conductor shift
items.statement: For an unramified irreducible generic local GL_n representation, the spherical Whittaker function for a conductor-zero character is nonzero at the identity. For a character from a canonical differential of local order n_v, conjugate by diag(varpi^−(n−1)n_v,...,1) to reduce to that case.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma5.3.3 proof pp37–38; Shintani76; Cogdell08 p116

uses.how: Input to Degree-zero nonvanishing of a spherical cusp form.

items.proofOutline: For a conductor-zero local additive character apply the spherical Whittaker formula at the identity. Conjugation by the specified diagonal transports a general residue-character conductor to that normalization. Check each root coordinate's valuation; Shintani/Cogdell originals are a source gate.
items.note: Review note: Faithful: J_v=(−(n−1)n_v,…,0) conjugates ψ_v on each simple-root coordinate by ϖ_v^{j_i−j_{i+1}}=ϖ_v^{−n_v}, giving the conductor-0 character ϖ_v^{−n_v}ψ_v. Shintani's formula is an unramified local calculation. It looks planned by AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3 ('unramified calculations') with SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.5 (Whittaker functionals), so 'planned' is arguable.

items.name: Cohomological tensor-duality identifications
items.statement: For lisse F1,F2 on the geometric curve, H0(F1⊗F2∨)=Hom(F2,F1), and H2(F1⊗F2∨)=Hom(F1,F2)∨(−1), Frobenius-equivariantly. Apply this to the orbit decomposition of a Weil representation to identify the self-pair H0/H2 polynomials.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Equations6.1.1–6.1.2 pp42–43, corrected E14

uses.how: Input to Cuspidal Rankin–Selberg degrees and poles.
Input to Self-pair functional equation and root radii.

items.proofOutline: Identify tensor sections with equivariant Hom(F2,F1). Apply proper-curve Poincare duality to the dual tensor for H2, obtaining Hom(F1,F2)^vee(−1). Track Frobenius through both identifications; this corrects the reversed Hom orders.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. F1⊗F2^∨ ≅ Hom(F2,F1) gives H^0(X, F1⊗F2^∨) = Hom_X(F2,F1). Poincaré duality on the proper curve gives H^2(X, F1⊗F2^∨) ≅ H^0(X, F1^∨⊗F2(1))^∨ = Hom_X(F1,F2)^∨(−1). Both identifications are canonical, hence Frobenius-equivariant for Weil sheaves on X_1. On 'planned': EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings states the pairing with coefficients E only. The lisse-coefficient form used here follows from EDC.1 Verdier duality and smooth purity, but that stage should name it.

items.name: Self-pair functional equation and root radii
items.statement: For a pure unitary cuspidal Weil system, the self-pair H1 has a symplectic pairing with multiplier q. Its numerator obeys P(z)=q^[(g−1)n²+d]z^[(2g−2)n²+2d]P(1/(qz)), and all roots have absolute value q^−1/2. The disjoint weights in H0,H1,H2 prevent cancellation with the denominator.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §6.1, pp. 42–43, Proposition 6.1.1 and its proof (symplectic pairing, ε), and the sentence after it (Lafforgue's Theorem VI.10: zeros of P on |z| = q^{−1/2}); §6.2.2, p. 46, equation (6.2.5)

uses.how: Input to Single-cycle normalizer evaluation.

items.proofOutline: Use Poincare duality on the self-dual tensor local system to obtain a symplectic H1 pairing with similitude q. Reciprocal eigenvalue pairs yield the functional equation, and purity gives their absolute values. Distinct H0/H1/H2 weights preclude common roots.
items.note: Review note: Statement checked: an alternating perfect pairing on H^1 with multiplier q makes the product of the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^1 equal to q^{N/2}, N = (2g−2)n² + 2d, hence P(z) = q^{N/2} z^N P(1/(qz)) and ε = q^{(g−1)n²}. missing is right. Route 4 sends it to AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.3, which plans the zeta-integral Rankin–Selberg theory (unramified computation, poles in the twist case) but not what this proof uses: the function-field degree (2g−2)n1n2 from the Euler characteristic, the purity separation of H0/H1/H2 and the epsilon value, all Galois-side through Lafforgue's correspondence (items 014, 042, 129, 130; EDC.2, DWP). Either AL.3 imports those or the item moves to the route-12 Part II.

items.name: Purity and point-count polynomial for stable Higgs moduli
items.statement: For a complex smooth projective curve and coprime (n,e), the cohomology of the stable Higgs moduli is pure, and its compact-support signed Poincare polynomial is t^[2(1+(g−1)n²)] A_g,n(t²,t,...,t). The spreading/point-count comparison and cohomological convention must be supplied from Hausel05 and Schiffmann16, not assumed from smoothness.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof p74; H05,Sc16 Corollary1.3

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.

items.proofOutline: Spread the coprime stable Higgs moduli to finite fields and compare its point-count polynomial with compact-support cohomology. Import the separate purity theorem and match signs, Tate powers and dimension. Neither smoothness alone nor the present reading proves this; H05/Sc16 originals are S6.

items.name: Nonabelian Hodge comparison in the twisted coprime case
items.statement: For a compact Riemann surface and coprime rank/degree, compare stable GL_n Higgs moduli with the twisted character variety with the matching central monodromy. The comparison yields the cohomological equality used for the Euler specialization; it is not an algebraic isomorphism of those moduli.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof; Simpson90 input

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.
Input to Euler characteristic of the twisted PGL_n character variety.

items.proofOutline: Use the coprime twisted nonabelian Hodge correspondence, with the prescribed central monodromy, to identify the relevant topological cohomology. It is not an algebraic isomorphism. The exact Simpson theorem and quotient compatibility have not been source-checked.

items.name: Euler characteristic of the twisted PGL_n character variety
items.statement: For g ≥ 2 and gcd(n,e) = 1, the twisted PGL_n character variety of a compact Riemann surface of genus g has Euler characteristic μ(n)n^{2g−3} [HR08, Cor. 1.1.1]. The GL_n/Jacobian quotient and the finite-group action must be matched to I_(g,n): the signed Poincaré polynomial satisfies P(M_(GL_n)) = (1−t)^{2g}P(M_(PGL_n)), and J_g(t²,t,…,t) = (1−t)^{2g}. Raw point counts must not be divided by a group order without this comparison.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof; HR08 Corollary1.1.1

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.

items.proofOutline: Import HR08's twisted PGL_n Euler calculation and check the finite group/Jacobian quotient comparison used to extract I_g,n from GL_n. The numerical formula is a source input, not justified by dividing arbitrary rational point counts.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: No genus hypothesis. For g = 1 and squarefree n ≥ 2 the value μ(n)n^{−1} is not an integer, so it cannot be an Euler characteristic; the only case used is g ≥ 2. The hypotheses of [HR08] were not re-read.

items.name: Ordinary locus and full symplectic monodromy of curve moduli
items.statement: In the tricanonically rigidified stable-curve moduli used by KS99 §10.6, the smooth locus is dense, the ordinary locus is nonempty open in every characteristic, and R1pi_!Q_l on the smooth universal family has geometric monodromy Sp_2g. The 3K structure is tricanonical rigidification, not an assumed prime-to-p level-three structure.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kob75 Theorem5; KS99 Theorems10.6.10–10.6.11

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.
Input to Larsen–Chavdarov maximal Weyl-group specialization input.

items.proofOutline: Construct the tricanonically rigidified universal curve family from KS99. Prove the ordinary locus nonempty via Koblitz and retain full symplectic geometric monodromy on the smooth open. These originals are not read; do not reinterpret 3K as level-three torsion.

items.name: Larsen–Chavdarov maximal Weyl-group specialization input
items.statement: For the universal curve family with full symplectic geometric monodromy, establish a density-one set of primes l with full mod-l Sp image, then the density of fibres whose zeta numerator has full Weyl Galois group. Yu uses Chavdarov's proof with infinitely many auxiliary primes instead of its printed almost-all hypothesis; this weakening needs a checked proof-level adapter.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kow06 Proposition3; Ch97 Theorem2.1

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.
Input to Ordinary maximal-Weyl eigenvalue independence.

items.proofOutline: Use Larsen's density-one residual full-monodromy primes and Chavdarov's sieve to produce maximal-Weyl zeta polynomials. Rerun the sieve proof under Yu's infinitely-many-primes hypothesis; quoting a theorem that assumes almost all primes is insufficient.

items.name: Ordinary maximal-Weyl eigenvalue independence
items.statement: For an ordinary curve with irreducible zeta numerator and full S_g⋉(S2)^g Galois group, a selected reciprocal half of the eigenvalues together with q is multiplicatively independent. The p-adic slopes are 0 and v_p(q); changing the chosen half permits any prescribed pattern of these valuations.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC; Kow06 Proposition1 proof andLemmas1–2

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.

items.proofOutline: Use the full signed-permutation Galois group to transport any eigenvalue multiplicative relation across single reciprocal swaps. Ordinary p-adic slopes force every exponent to vanish after separating the q exponent. Check Kowalski's original argument and its irreducibility hypothesis.
items.note: Review note: Checked. With Galois group W_g acting on the roots, Q^{2g} = 1 ⊕ Std_(g−1) ⊕ Sgn_g as W_g-modules, each summand of multiplicity one. The relation lattice is W-stable and contains Std. Ordinarity excludes Sgn, since σ_i/σ_(i+g) is not a unit at p. The trivial summand is excluded because q is not a root of unity. The lattice ⟨f_i − f_j⟩ is saturated, so independence holds exactly, not only modulo roots of unity.

items.name: Genus-one ordinary existence for the cone test
items.statement: For every prime p, the polynomial X²+X+p is an ordinary elliptic Weil polynomial and Honda–Tate realizes it by an elliptic curve over Fp. Its paired roots and p provide the multiplicative independence needed by item121.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.

items.proofOutline: Check X²+X+p is an ordinary elliptic Weil polynomial: its discriminant is negative and its trace −1 is prime to p. Apply the ordinary elliptic case of Honda–Tate, then use the two opposite p-adic slopes to verify independence of p and a chosen root.
items.note: Review note: Statement checked. Existence also follows from Deuring and Waterhouse (every t with |t| ≤ 2√p and p ∤ t is the trace of an elliptic curve over F_p), here with t = −1. No atlas stage plans it; the Tau Ceti EllipticCurves roadmap has only the Hasse bound.

items.name: Stack mass and rational stable Higgs objects
items.statement: For a finite groupoid define its mass as Σ_[x]1/|Aut(x)|. In the coprime stable Higgs case, show the rational-point/coarse-object comparison and scalar automorphism group before using mass=#Higgs^st(Fq)/(q−1). This is the precise conversion in AppendixB.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixB p79

uses.how: Input to Higgs count and geometrically indecomposable bundles.

items.name: Explicit rank-two and rank-three recurrence checks
items.statement: For g ≠ 1, Théorème 1.2 with e = 1 gives: 𝒫_1^1(X_1) = C_1(X_1); 𝒫_2^1(X_1) = C_2(X_1) + (g−1)C_1(X_1)² + C_1(X_1); 𝒫_3^1(X_1) = C_3(X_1) + 4(g−1)C_1(X_1)C_2(X_1) + (g−1)C_1(X_1)C_1(X_2) + 2(g−1)²C_1(X_1)³ + 2(g−1)C_1(X_1)² + C_1(X_1). By Théorème A.4 in the coprime case, the same identities hold for 𝒫_n^e(X_1) with any e prime to n.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §1 examples p5
items.proofOutline: Expand the recurrence through degrees two and three, retain constant-extension Adams terms, and solve the coefficient-one C_n equation. Check each partition and its multiplicity; the rank-three expression includes C1(X2) separately from C1(X1).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-YU-23): statement corrected against the paper: Notation. These identities concern 𝒫_n^1(X_1), the number of isocline bundles of rank n and degree 1 (equal to J_1 by Théorème 1.3), not the local-system polynomials P_(g,n). C_m(X_k) is the absolutely cuspidal count. Review note: Verified symbolically with sympy, g symbolic: expanding the formula of Théorème 1.2 for n = 1, 2, 3 reproduces all three examples exactly. These identities were then used to generate P_(g,2) and P_(g,3) for the end-to-end integrality check (item 108).

items.name: Vandermonde determinant and invertibility criterion
items.statement: For a finite vector v over a commutative ring, det(vandermonde v)=∏_i ∏_(j>i)(v_j−v_i). In an integral domain this determinant is nonzero exactly when v is injective. Over a field this makes the consecutive-power system invertible.

items.name: Haar probability preserved by a surjective homomorphism
items.statement: A continuous surjective homomorphism f:G→*H, with H a compact topological group, Borel measurable spaces and Haar measures of equal total mass, is measure preserving. Use probability Haar on all compact character groups, including disconnected ones.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Normalized transfer along a finite compact-group cover.

items.proofOutline: Import MonoidHom.measurePreserving at the pin; discharge continuity, surjectivity and equal mass before applying it to multiplication or mu_w. No factor equal to the covering degree belongs in Haar pushforward.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Read at Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Haar/Unique.lean:951: MonoidHom.measurePreserving. Its hypotheses are G a topological group with Borel σ-algebra, H a compact topological group with Borel σ-algebra, Haar measures μ, ν with μ univ=ν univ, and f continuous and surjective; its conclusion is MeasurePreserving f μ ν. This is exactly the item. It is used for u_F in Lemme 4.2.5, for the multiplication Im X_L^G×Im X_M^L → Im X_M^G (p. 35) and for μ_w (item 147), all with probability Haar measures.

items.name: Cycle coordinates for the spectral character cover
items.statement: Let w permute equal-rank blocks of M. Index its nonempty cycles by j, with length l_j≥1 and common block rank d_j≥1; N_j=l_j*d_j and n=ΣN_j. In unit-circle coordinates z_(j,t), define T by ∏_(j,t)z_(j,t)^d_j=1; A consists of cycle-constant u_j with ∏u_j^N_j=1; B satisfies ∏_t v_(j,t)^d_j=1 separately for each j, and B0 satisfies ∏_t v_(j,t)=1 separately. Embed A and B in T. These are respectively Im X_M^G, Im X_L^G, Im X_M^L and its identity component, L=L_w.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Checked. With X_M=(C^×)^{blocks} (4.1.5), X_M^G is cut out by ∏z_{j,t}^{d_j}=1. X_L^G restricted to M is cycle-constant (the L-block determinant restricts to the product of M-block determinants) with ∏u_j^{N_j}=1. X_M^L (trivial on Z_L(A); a degree-one scalar in L-block j has multidegree d_j on each of its M-blocks) is ∏_t v_{j,t}^{d_j}=1 for each j, and its identity component is ∏_t v_{j,t}=1 for each j. The blocks of L_w are the unions along cycles, because a_{L_w}=ker(w−1)|a_M consists of the cycle-constant vectors. A ⊂ T and B ⊂ T hold.

items.name: Difference map on every Weyl cycle
items.statement: For the groups in145, δ_w:B→B0, v↦v/w⁻¹(v), is surjective, with kernel ∏_j μ_(N_j). Every fibre has ∏_j N_j points, even when B is disconnected.

items.proofOutline: Choose an orientation of each cycle. For b with product one, solve v_t/v_(t−1)=b_t recursively from v_0=c. The final cyclic equation is exactly ∏b_t=1. The condition (∏v_t)^d=1 is an equation c^(ld)=a in Circle, which has exactly ld distinct solutions. For b=1 all v_t=c and c^(ld)=1. Product over cycles; a reverse orientation gives the same cardinality.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. δ_w(v)_{j,t}=v_{j,t}/v_{j,σ(t)} has cycle products 1, so it lands in B0. Given b in B0, the equations c_t/c_{t+1}=b_t are consistent (∏b_t=1) and determine c from c_1; the condition defining B becomes c_1^{l_jd_j}=κ_j for a fixed κ_j (l_jd_j=N_j), so each fibre has N_j points per cycle and the kernel is the cycle-constant c with c^{N_j}=1, i.e. ∏μ_{N_j}=X_L^L. This is the paper's claim 'noyau Im X_L^L=X_L^L' (p. 35), made explicit.

items.name: Degree and fibres of the spectral cover
items.statement: The continuous homomorphism mu_w:A×B→T, (a,c)↦a*δ_w(c), is onto with |ker mu_w|=D=(∏l_j)(∏N_j)=|w|*|X_L^L|. For any tau∈T its fibre consists of the finite pairs a∈A, b∈B0 with tau=a*b, followed by c∈B with δ_w(c)=b. There are ∏l_j outer pairs and ∏N_j inner lifts.

items.proofOutline: For tau choose u_j with u_j^l_j=∏_t tau_(j,t). Then ∏u_j^N_j=1, so a∈A and b=tau/a∈B0. Choices of a differ by A∩B0=∏μ_(l_j). Apply146 to b. Fibres are translates of the kernel. The notation |w| means product of cycle lengths, not permutation order.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Onto: given τ, choose u_j with u_j^{l_j}=∏_tτ_{j,t}. Then ∏u_j^{N_j}=∏_{j,t}τ_{j,t}^{d_j}=1, so u is in A, and τ/u is in B0. The outer choices are exactly these u (∏l_j of them), since τ/a in B0 forces a_j^{l_j}=∏_tτ_{j,t}. The inner lifts number ∏N_j (item 146). The kernel has order |A∩B0|·|ker δ_w|=(∏l_j)(∏N_j)=|w||X_L^L|. This agrees with p. 35 ('(Im X_M^L)°∩Im X_L^G a pour cardinal |w|').

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. A continuous surjective homomorphism of compact Lie groups with finite kernel is open (open mapping theorem) and a local diffeomorphism (finite kernel makes dp injective, and equal dimensions make it bijective). So Tr_pf(y)=D^{-1}Σ_{k in F}f(s(y)k) with s a local smooth section, which is continuous or smooth when f is. With probability Haar measures, ∫_K Tr_pf·g=∫_H f·(g∘p). This is the integral-preservation property the report uses and item 149 needs; the item statement could add it explicitly.

items.name: Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average
items.statement: For p:H→K as in148 and smooth complex f on H, at every y∈K the absolutely convergent character sum Σ_(χ∈Khat) ∫_H χ(p(x)/y)*f(x) dx equals Tr_p f(y). Equivalently the coefficient indexed by χ is the (χ⁻¹)-Fourier coefficient of Tr_p f. Apply p=mu_w and y=lambda_pi to obtain (5.2.12) with factor D⁻¹.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.

items.proofOutline: Kernel averaging and142 give ∫_H χ(p(x))f(x)=∫_K χ(z)Tr_p f(z). A compact abelian Lie group is a finite abelian group times a torus; for these explicit tori obtain such coordinates from their integer exponent matrices. Combine finite character orthogonality144 and torus inversion143. Item150 supplies absolute summability. Reindex χ to χ⁻¹ to get the displayed sign. This is pointwise evaluation of a smooth function, not evaluation of an L² equivalence class.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. ∫_Hχ(p(x)/y)f(x)dx=χ(y)^{-1}∫_Kχ·Tr_pf is the Fourier coefficient of Tr_pf at χ^{-1} (item 148 with g=χ). Summing over χ in K̂ gives Tr_pf(y) by pointwise inversion on K≅torus×finite abelian group (items 143, 144 and the structure theorem for compact abelian Lie groups), and the sum converges absolutely by item 150 applied to the smooth Tr_pf. With p=μ_w and y=λ_π this is (5.2.12) with 1/|ker μ_w|. The identity needs probability Haar measures on H and K, which the paper leaves implicit (new issue).

items.name: Smooth Fourier decay on the character groups in the trace formula
items.statement: On a finite product of Circle and a finite abelian group, a smooth complex function has absolutely summable Fourier coefficients. For torus dimension d and integer s with 2s>d, |fhat(k)|≤C(1+4π²||k||²)^(-s). The statement includes dimension zero and is uniform in a compact auxiliary parameter when the corresponding derivatives are uniformly bounded.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.

items.proofOutline: Apply (1−Δ)^s to the periodic smooth function and integrate by parts on each circle; boundary terms cancel. Bound the Fourier coefficient by its L¹ norm to get the displayed estimate. Count lattice points in sup-norm shells to sum (1+||k||²)^(-s). There are only finitely many component characters. For parameter families bound finitely many derivatives on the compact product. Integer-lattice coordinate decomposition and derivative transport remain implementation adapters, not an imported library theorem.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. Integration by parts with (1−Δ)^s on (R/Z)^d gives (1+4π²|k|²)^s f̂(k)=((1−Δ)^s f)^(k), so |f̂(k)|≤‖(1−Δ)^s f‖_{L¹}(1+4π²|k|²)^{−s}. The sum Σ_k(1+|k|²)^{−s} is finite exactly when 2s>d. A finite abelian factor adds finitely many characters, and d=0 is trivial. Uniformity in a compact parameter holds under uniform bounds on the derivatives of order ≤2s.

items.name: Typed finite-fibre operator trace
items.statement: For a discrete pair (P,pi), (w,tau)∈stab(P,pi), L=L_w, a∈A, b∈B0, tau=a*b and c∈B with δ_w(c)=b, put z=lambda*c for lambda∈A. Define R_Q(z;v)=M_(R|P)(z)⁻¹∘M_(R|P)(z/v), where R∈P^Q(M), v∈X_L^G. For h_Q=hat1_Q(·eta⁻¹) or hat1_Q^e, set F_h(lambda,a,c)=lim_(mu→1 in X_L^G) Tr_(A_P,pi)[(Σ_(Q∈P(L))h_Q(mu*a) R_Q(z;mu*a))∘M(w,w⁻¹(c))∘U_tau]. U_tau is multiplication by tau. The Q-sum is continued holomorphically before evaluation at mu=1; the other parameters are unitary.

items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound as a definition, contingent on imported analytic facts. It matches (5.2.9)/(5.2.14) with a=λ_L, b=λ^L, c=λ_w, z=λλ_w and U_τ=·λ_π, and the operator order (family ∘ M(w,w^{-1}(c)) ∘ U_τ) is the paper's. items.name: Degree Fourier recovery of the spectral contribution
items.statement: Let n>0, zeta primitive of order n and eta=zeta^deg. If J_(eta^k)=Σ_(e mod n)zeta^(ek) J_e, then J_e=n⁻¹Σ_(k mod n)zeta^(−ek)J_(eta^k). In151 this replaces hat1_Q(mu*a*eta^(−k)) by hat1_Q^e(mu*a)=n⁻¹Σ_k zeta^(ek)hat1_Q(mu*a*eta^k), leaving the fibre, operator order and denominator unchanged. It holds for every integer e, not just coprime e.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

items.proofOutline: Apply finite character orthogonality144 to Z/nZ. Interchange only finite sums with integrals and the regularized limit, then substitute k↦−k in the cone-series term. Coprimality is used later in067, not in this recovery.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound. J_{η^k}=Σ_{e mod n}ζ^{ek}J_e follows from (5.2.8), and inversion follows from finite orthogonality. Substituting gives n^{-1}Σ_kζ^{−ek}1̂_Q(vη^{−k})=n^{-1}Σ_kζ^{ek}1̂_Q(vη^k)=1̂^e_Q(v) after k ↦ −k mod n; nothing else in the integrand depends on η. This matches Corollaire 5.2.3, stated for all e in Z. The hypothesis 'J_{η^k}=Σζ^{ek}J_e' is itself (5.2.8), which needs its own item (coverage entry below).

items.name: Explicit transport between induction normalization conventions
items.statement: Fix positive inducing characters s_R on M(A). Define A_R,pi^s by s_R⁻¹*phi|_M∈pi and spherical basis phi_R(nmk)=s_R(m)*phi_pi(m). For a second convention t_R, C_R^(s→t) multiplies by t_R/s_R in Iwasawa coordinates. Transport each operator by M^t_(R′|R)=C_R′ M^s_(R′|R) C_R⁻¹. Yu p32 and Laf97 p284 use s_R=rho_R in their membership formula (Yu writes P); Yu p39 uses s_R=rho_R⁻¹. One cannot identify their numerical normalizers until this dictionary, including parameter conventions, is checked.

items.testStatus: Planning specifications, not Lean elaborated; exact diagnostics in the report cover only their named bounded arithmetic instances.
items.note: Review note: REPAIR VERDICT: sound, with one caveat. C_R^{s→t} (multiplication by (t_R/s_R)(m(g))) is well defined because t_R/s_R is trivial on M(F)M(O), and it maps A^s_{R,π} onto A^t_{R,π}. The conjugated operator C_{R'}M^sC_R^{-1} is the operator defined by transport, but it is not the integral (5.2.6) on A^t at the same λ. With ν=t_R/s_R in Re X_M, the integral on t-sections at λ corresponds to the s-integral at λν, up to the character relating t_{R'}/s_{R'} and w(ν). So the dictionary must include the parameter shift, as the item's last sentence says. For s=ρ_R and t=ρ_R^{-1} the shift ρ_R^{-2} turns L(z)/L(q^{-1}z) into L(q^2z)/L(qz) (GL_2 check). This identifies s_R=ρ_R as the convention matching (5.1.1) and settles the S2 question in favour of p32 (with R for P).

items.name: Coprime trace equals Mellit's polynomial
items.statement: If (e, n) = 1, then J^e = A_{g,n}(q, σ_1, …, σ_g).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Corollaire 3.2.6 p.18
items.note: Added by cc-442dc5: a numbered statement without its own item. Combine Theorem 3.2.4 (item 034) with Theorem 3.2.5 (items 037, 046). Review note: Fine. 'J^e' in the statement means Yu's J_e = J_e^{T=0} (the T = 0 value), not J^T; the notation should match the other items. Status missing is right. Locator p. 18 checked.

items.name: Lafforgue's cutoff formula for the truncated unit-test-function trace
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1, e ∈ Z and T ∈ 𝔞_B with d(T) = min_{α∈Δ_B} α(T) ≥ max(2g−2, 0). Let F^G(·, T) be the characteristic function of those g ∈ G(F)\G(A)/K such that τ̂_P(H_P(δg) − T) = 0 for every proper standard parabolic P ⊊ G and every δ ∈ P(F)\G(F) (E1). Then J^T_e = ∫_{G(F)\G(A)^e} F^G(g, T) Σ_{γ∈G(F)} 1_K(g^{−1}γg) dg, where J^T_e is the truncated integral (3.2.2).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.1, p. 18, equation (3.3.1); [Laf97, Proposition 11, p. 227]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Key step of Théorème 3.2.4: it turns the truncated trace into the count of T-semistable bundles. Items 024/025 cite Laf97 p. 227 only for convergence, and item 033 assumes the cutoff form without stating it. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: The cutoff F^G(·, T) is the indicator of T-semistable bundles
items.statement: Let T ∈ 𝔞_B with T_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ T_n. (a) (Remarque 3.3.2) F^G(g, T) = 1 if and only if τ̂_P(H_P(δg) − T) = 0 for all maximal standard P (M_P ≅ G_r × G_{n−r}) and all δ ∈ P(F)\G(F), because τ̂_P(H_P(δg) − T) = 1 implies τ̂_Q(H_Q(δg) − T) = 1 for every Q ⊇ P, as Δ̂_Q ⊆ Δ̂_P. (b) Under the bundle–adele dictionary, a pair (P, δ) with P standard of block ranks summing to N_1 < ⋯ < N_k = n corresponds to a flag 0 = F_0 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ F_k = E^g with H_P(δg) = (deg(F_i/F_{i−1}))_i, and τ̂_P(H_P(δg) − T) = 1 if and only if every F_i with 0 < i < k violates deg(F_i)/N_i − (T_1+⋯+T_{N_i})/N_i ≤ deg(E^g)/n − (T_1+⋯+T_n)/n. (c) Hence F^G(g, T) = 1 if and only if E^g is T-semistable.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.1, pp. 18–19, (3.3.2), Remarque 3.3.2 and the paragraph containing (3.3.5)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Needed to read (3.3.1) as the number of T-semistable bundles. No item states the equivalence between F^G(g,T) = 1 and E^g being T-semistable. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Quasi-polynomiality of the Γ-lattice counts and determination from the deep chamber
items.statement: Let M_P ≅ GL(n_1) × ⋯ × GL(n_r), e ∈ Z and e_i ∈ Z/n_iZ, and let h = h^e_{(e_i)} = {(d_1, …, d_r) ∈ Z^r : Σ d_i = e, d_i ≡ e_i mod n_i}. (a) [Ch15, Prop 4.5.5] On lattice points T ∈ Hom(X^*(B), Z) ≅ Z^n with T_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ T_n, the finite sum T ↦ Σ_{H∈h} Γ_{(n_1,…,n_r)}(H, T) agrees with a quasi-polynomial Σ_{ν∈f} p_ν(T) q^{⟨ν,T⟩}, with f ⊂ (2πi/log q) X^*(B) ⊗ Q finite and each p_ν a polynomial. Yu's Γ_I equals Chaudouard's Γ_P. (b) Two such quasi-polynomials that agree at all lattice points T with d(T) ≥ c agree on all lattice points of the closed chamber, in particular at T = 0. (c) (Remarque 3.3.3) Γ_I(·, 0) ≡ 0 for r > 1 and Γ_{(n)} ≡ 1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.1, p. 20, and Remarque 3.3.3, p. 19; [Ch15, Définition 4.5.3, Proposition 4.5.5]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the continuation step that lets Yu set T = 0. Item 025 covers only the left side (Théorème 3.3.1). The right-hand lattice counts and the principle that a quasi-polynomial is determined by its values deep in the chamber are not items. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Harder: common compact-mod-centre support of unramified cusp forms
items.statement: There is a subset Ω ⊂ G(F)\G(A), compact modulo Z_G(A), containing the support of every right-K-invariant function φ on G(F)\G(A) whose constant terms ∫_{N_P(F)\N_P(A)} φ(ng) dn vanish for every proper standard parabolic P. Consequently, for every central character θ, A_{G,θ,cusp} is finite-dimensional and contained in L²(G(F)\G(A))_θ^K. Together with the finiteness of Pic^0(X_k), up to twists by X_G only finitely many central characters occur, so C_n(X_k) is finite.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §1.2, p. 4; §2.3.1, p. 9; Remarque 3 after Définition 2.3.4, p. 11; [Ha74, 1.2.1]
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Used for the finiteness of C_n(X_k) (so for item 016) and for 'cuspidal ⇒ discrete' (item 017). No item states it.

items.name: F. K. Schmidt: the degree map of a curve over a finite field is surjective
items.statement: Let X_1 be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over F_q with function field F. The degree map deg: A^× → Z, deg(g) = −Σ_x [κ(x):F_q] x(g_x), is surjective; equivalently, X_1 has a divisor, hence a line bundle, of degree 1. No F_q-rational point is assumed.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §2.2.3, p. 9 (choice of a); used in §3.3.1, p. 20
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): The existence of a degree-one idele is a theorem, and Ξ_M, X_M^L and the periodicity of P_n^e all depend on it. Item 009 says 'choose' without citing it. Route: FunctionFieldArithmetic.

items.name: Periodicity of the isocline count in the degree
items.statement: Let L be a line bundle of degree 1 on X_1 (F. K. Schmidt). Then E ↦ E ⊗ L is a bijection from isomorphism classes of isocline bundles of rank n and degree e to those of rank n and degree e + n, since it preserves direct-sum decompositions and shifts every slope by 1. Hence P_n^{e+n}(X_1) = P_n^e(X_1), and P_n^e(X_1) depends only on e mod n.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Used to regroup the Γ-sum by degrees modulo ranks. It is elementary but needs a degree-one line bundle, and it is not an item. It is distinct from Théorème 1.4 (item 119), which concerns the order of e. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Local constant-term (Satake) homomorphism t_P
items.statement: For a standard parabolic P and a closed point x, and f ∈ H_{G,x}, set t_P(f)(m) = ρ_P(m) ∫_{N_P(F_x)} f(mn) dn for m ∈ M_P(F_x), where ρ_P is the positive square root of the modulus character (m·dn·m^{−1} = ρ_P(m)² dn). Then t_P(f) ∈ H_{M_P,x}, and t_P: H_{G,x} → H_{M_P,x} is an algebra homomorphism, making H_{M_P,x} an H_{G,x}-algebra and every H_{M_P}-module an H_G-module. The character |·|: G(A) → C^× is |g| = q^{deg(det g)}. The local Haar measure on N_P(F_x) is not stated by Yu; vol(N_P(O_x)) = 1 is the natural choice.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Théorème 2.3.6 (item 020) is stated through t_P, which no item defines.

items.name: Automorphic inertial twists, Fix(π) and inertial equivalence
items.statement: For π ∈ A_n(X_1) and λ ∈ X_G, π ⊗ λ is the H_G-module {g ↦ φ(g)λ(g) : φ ∈ π}. Fix(π) = {λ ∈ X_G : π ⊗ λ = π}. Comparing central characters gives λ(a)^n = 1, so Fix(π) is cyclic of order dividing n. By multiplicity one, π ⊗ λ ≅ π as H_G-modules if and only if the two subspaces are equal (Remarque 2.3.1). π_1, π_2 ∈ A_n(X_1) are inertially equivalent if π_1 ⊗ λ = π_2 for some λ ∈ X_G (Définition 2.3.2). For a discrete everywhere-unramified π of M(A), Fix(π) = {λ ∈ X_M : π ⊗ λ = π} ⊆ X_M^M is finite.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): C_n(X_k) (item 015), Corollaire 2.3.3 (item 016) and the stabilizers (items 018, 021) all use the automorphic twist action and Fix(π). Item 004 defines only the Galois-side version. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Frobenius pullback is conjugation by a geometric-Frobenius lift
items.statement: Fix a section j: Z → W(X_1, o) of the degree map. For an ℓ-adic representation σ of π_1(X, o), let σ^{j(1)}(h) = σ(j(1) h j(1)^{−1}). The isomorphism class of σ^{j(1)} does not depend on j. Under the equivalence between lisse Q̄_ℓ-sheaves on X and ℓ-adic representations of π_1(X, o), σ^{j(1)} corresponds to F_X^* of the sheaf of σ. So conjugation by j(1) on isomorphism classes coincides with F_X^* on E_n.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Item 005 ('extends iff its class is F_X-fixed') depends on this comparison between the Frobenius endomorphism and the geometric Frobenius element, and no item states it. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Twisted truncated trace and its degree decomposition
items.statement: Let n≥1, ζ an n-th root of unity and η=ζ^{deg det} in X_G^G. Define J^T_η:=∫_{G(F)\G(A)/Ξ_G} η(g)k^T(g,g)dg, with k^T Arthur's truncated kernel (item 024) and Ξ_G=a^Z (a a fixed idele of degree 1, as a scalar matrix, so deg det a=n). Since G(F) ⊂ G(A)^0, k^T(g,g) is Ξ_G-invariant, and G(F)\G(A)^e → G(F)\G(A)/Ξ_G is a measure-preserving bijection onto the classes with deg det ≡ e (mod n), one has J^T_η=Σ_{e=1}^n ζ^e J^T_e with J^T_e=∫_{G(F)\G(A)^e}k^T(x,x)dx, and J^T_e depends only on e mod n. Hence, for ζ primitive, J^T_{η^k}=Σ_{e=1}^nζ^{ek}J^T_e for all k in Z and J^T_e=n^{-1}Σ_{k=1}^nζ^{−ek}J^T_{η^k} for all e in Z.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §5.2.3, p. 33, equation (5.2.8); p. 36, displays before Corollaire 5.2.3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): The degree decomposition J_η=Σζ^eJ_e is the hypothesis of item 152 and the starting point of Théorème 5.2.2, but no item defines J^T_η or proves the decomposition. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Lafforgue's spectral expansion before Fourier inversion, twisted by η
items.statement: (Lafforgue 1997, VI §2, through Lemme 9 and Corollaire 10, with the change of variable μ_Q ↦ μ_Qη^{-1} at the start of step (e), p. 304.) For G=GL_n over the function field F of X_1 and η in X_G^G, J_η=J_η^{T=0} equals the sum, over inertial classes of everywhere-unramified discrete pairs (P,π) and over continuous characters χ of Im X_{M_P}^G, of |stab(P,π)|^{-1}Σ_{(w,λ_π) in stab(P,π)} lim_{μ0 in X_{L_w}^G, μ0→1} Σ_{Q in P(L_w)} ∫_{Im X_{L_w}^G}∫_{Im X_{M_P}^G} 1̂_Q(μμ0η^{-1}) χ(λ w(λ_π)μ0μ/w(λ)) Tr_{A_{P,π}}(M_Q(λ,P;μμ0) ∘ M(w^{-1},w(λ)) ∘ w(λ_π)^{-1}) dλ dμ, with probability Haar measures. The Q-sum is continued holomorphically as a whole before μ0→1 (Laf97 Corollaire 10), using the isometry of intertwiners on the unitary axis, the functional equation, and the relations w(λ0)^{H_P}M(w,λ)φ=M(w,λλ0^{-1})(φλ0^{H_P}) and M(w,λμ)=M(w,λ) for μ in X_{L_w}^G.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §5.2.3, p. 34, proof of Théorème 5.2.2, equation (5.2.10)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the only analytic input of item 063 that is not an item: the coarse spectral expansion of Lafforgue before Fourier inversion, adapted to η. E9 and S2 refer to it but nothing states it. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Residual discrete forms are residues of cuspidal Eisenstein series
items.statement: (Langlands; Moeglin–Waldspurger 1994, V.3.13(iii).) Let π be an everywhere-unramified discrete, non-cuspidal automorphic representation of G_n(A). For every φ in π there are a discrete pair (P',π') all of whose factors are cuspidal, a cuspidal φ' in A_{P',π'} and a point λ' in X_{P'}^G such that φ(g)=Res_{λ'}E(φ',·)(g) for all g in G(A), where E(φ',λ) is the Eisenstein series of φ' (MW94 II.1.5) and Res_{λ'} is an iterated residue operator at λ'. Moreover E(φ'λ0,λ)=λ0·E(φ',λ) for λ0 in X_G^G.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §5.3.1, pp. 38–39, proof of Proposition 5.3.1 (citing [MW94, V.3.13(iii)] and [MW94, II.1.5])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): The residual case of Proposition 5.3.1 rests on this theorem. Item 065 mentions 'the Eisenstein residue construction', but no item states it, and item 020 (MW classification) does not supply it.

items.name: Additive character from a canonical divisor with exact local conductors
items.statement: Let D=Σ_v n_v v be a canonical divisor of X_1 (deg D=2g−2), fix uniformizers ϖ_v and put u=(ϖ_v^{−n_v})_v in A^×. Serre duality and geometric connectedness give A/(F+uO) ≅ H^1(X_1,O(D)) ≅ H^0(X_1,O_{X_1})^∨ ≅ F_q. Composing with a nontrivial character of F_q gives a nontrivial character ψ=⊗'_vψ_v of A/F, trivial on uO. For every v, ψ_v is trivial on ϖ_v^{−n_v}O_v but not on ϖ_v^{−n_v−1}O_v: otherwise ψ would factor through A/(F+u'O) ≅ H^1(X_1,O(D+v)) ≅ H^0(X_1,O(−v))^∨=0. Hence a ↦ ψ_v(ϖ_v^{−n_v}a) has conductor 0.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Items 127 and 128 assume 'a character from a canonical differential of local order n_v'. The construction and the exactness of the conductors, which Yu proves, are not itemized.

items.name: Unramified Rankin–Selberg L-function of a pair of discrete representations
items.statement: For everywhere-unramified discrete automorphic representations Π of G_a(A) and Π' of G_b(A), with Satake parameters (z_{v,1},…,z_{v,a}) and (z'_{v,1},…,z'_{v,b}) at each closed point v, put L(Π×Π'^∨,z)=∏_{v in |X_1|}∏_{k=1}^a∏_{l=1}^b(1−z_{v,k}z'^{-1}_{v,l}z^{deg v})^{-1} in C[[z]]. It converges for |z| small and is a rational function of z ([Laf02, App. B]). For unitary Π, Π' one has Π^∨≅Π̄, hence L(Π'×Π^∨,z)=conj(L(Π×Π'^∨,z̄)), and the two functions have the same numbers of zeros and poles in |z|<1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §5.1.2, p. 30 (citing [Laf02, Appendice B])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Every n_β and all of (c) are built from this L-function, but no item defines the everywhere-unramified Rankin–Selberg L-function of pairs of discrete representations or records the conjugation symmetry the zero and pole counts rely on. Item 042 is the cohomological side, not this definition. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.

items.name: Arthur's root-basis identity for θ-sums
items.statement: Let m=dim a_M^G and β_1,…,β_m distinct elements of Φ(Z_M,G). For ξ in a_{M,C}^* with ⟨ξ,α^∨⟩≠0 for all α in Φ(Z_M,G), Σ'_Q θ_Q(ξ)^{-1}∏_{j=1}^m⟨ξ,β_j^∨⟩, summed over the Q in P(M) with {β_1,…,β_m} ⊆ Φ_Q, equals 0 if the β_j are linearly dependent and 1 if they form a basis of a_M^{G,*}. Here θ_Q is Yu's unnormalized θ_Q. In type A every basis of relative coroots generates the full lattice {x in Z^r: Σx=0}, so Arthur's volume factors cancel.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §4.2.3, p. 26, proof of Théorème 4.2.4 (citing [Ar82, pp. 1319–1320])
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): The k=m step of the proof of Théorème 4.2.4 (item 052) imports this identity from Arthur, and no item states it. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Euler product for residual Rankin–Selberg L-functions
items.statement: Let π be an everywhere-unramified cuspidal automorphic representation of G_d(A), ν ≥ 1, and Π = π ⊠ ν the discrete representation of G_{dν}(A) of Theorem 2.3.6. For every everywhere-unramified discrete automorphic representation Π' of some G_{d'}(A), L(Π × Π'^∨, z) = ∏_{i=1}^{ν} L(π × Π'^∨, q^{(ν+1)/2 − i} z) as rational functions of z. Hence for Π_k = π_k ⊠ ν_k, L(Π1×Π2^∨, z) = ∏_{i=1}^{ν1}∏_{j=1}^{ν2} L(π1×π2^∨, q^{(ν1+ν2)/2+1−i−j} z). If ν1 ≥ ν2, then L(Π1×Π2^∨, z)/L(Π1×Π2^∨, q^{−1}z) = ∏_{i=1}^{ν2} L(π1×π2^∨, q^{(ν1+ν2)/2−i} z) / ∏_{i=1}^{ν2} L(π1×π2^∨, q^{−(ν1+ν2)/2+i−1} z).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §6.1, pp. 43–44, Lemme 6.1.3 and equation (6.1.5)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): A separate declaration (an Euler-product identity), used by Corollary 6.1.2 and again through (6.1.5) in the §6.2.2 formula for n_β. It is covered only inside item 069. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.

items.name: Reflection formula for the self-pair normalising factor
items.statement: Let π0 be a unitary everywhere-unramified cuspidal automorphic representation of G_r(A), f = |Fix(π0)|, ν ≥ 1, and Π0 = π0 ⊠ ν of rank d = rν. Write L(π0×π0^∨, z) = P(z)/Q(z) with P(0) = 1, so Q(z) = (1−z^f)(1−(qz)^f) and P(z) = q^{(g−1)r²+f} z^{(2g−2)r²+2f} P(1/(qz)) (item 130). Put n_β(z) = q^{(1−g)d²} L(Π0×Π0^∨, z)/L(Π0×Π0^∨, q^{−1}z). Then, as rational functions, n_β(z) = q^{(1−g)d²} ∏_{i=1}^{ν} P(q^{i−1}z)/P(q^{−i}z) · ∏_{i=1}^{ν} (1−(q^{−i}z)^f)/(1−(q^{i}z)^f) · ∏_{i=1}^{ν−1} (1−(q^{−i}z)^f)/(1−(q^{i}z)^f) = −z^{E} F(1/z)/F(z), where E = ((2g−2)r²+4f)ν − f and F(z) = ∏_{i=1}^{ν} P(q^{−i}z) · ∏_{i=1}^{ν}(1−(q^{i}z)^f) · ∏_{i=1}^{ν−1}(1−(q^{i}z)^f). F is a polynomial in z^f with no zero on |z| = 1. Hence n_β(μz) = n_β(z) for μ^f = 1, n_β(z) n_β(1/z) = 1, and ∏_{s=2}^{l} n_β(λ^{s−1}) = (−1)^{l−1} λ^{E l(l−1)/2} whenever λ^{lf} = 1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §6.2.2, p. 46, the display after 'Par (6.1.5)' and equation (6.2.6)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This reflection formula for the self-pair normalising factor is the crux of item 071 and the carrier of the sign in E19; it sits only inside 071's proof. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.

items.name: Zero–pole index in the open unit disc
items.statement: For f meromorphic on a neighbourhood of the closed unit disc (in the paper, a rational function of z), N(f) and P(f) are the numbers of zeros and poles of f in D = {|z| < 1}, counted with multiplicity, and (N−P)(f) = Σ_{a∈D} ord_a(f). API: (N−P)(fg) = (N−P)(f) + (N−P)(g) and (N−P)(1/f) = −(N−P)(f) for f, g not identically zero; (N−P)(c·f) = (N−P)(f) for c ≠ 0; for a polynomial R with R(0) ≠ 0 and c ≠ 0, (N−P)(z ↦ R(cz)) is the number of roots w of R, with multiplicity, with |w| < |c|.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §6.1, p. 43, Corollaire 6.1.2 (notation N(f), P(f)); used in Proposition 5.1.1(c), p. 31, and Théorème 6.4.1, p. 53
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): No item defines the zero–pole index, yet Corollary 6.1.2 and Theorem 6.4.1 rely on its additivity over products and quotients of shifted L-factors, and on its behaviour under z ↦ cz. Route: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.

items.name: Stabiliser order of a good pair
items.statement: If (P,π̃) is a good representative with π̃ = ⊗_i Π_i^{⊗m_i} (the Π_i pairwise not inertially equivalent), then stab(P,π̃) = {(w,λ) : w ∈ ∏_i S_{m_i}, λ ∈ Fix(π̃)} and |stab(P,π̃)| = ∏_i m_i! |Fix(Π_i)|^{m_i}. For a cuspidal pair grouped by rank j, |Fix| = d and multiplicity i (item 091), 1/|stab(P,π̃)| = ∏_{j≥1}∏_{d|j} 1/(d^{k_d^j} ∏_{i≥1}(i!)^{b_{d,i}^j}).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §6.6.2, p. 60, equation (6.6.7); §2.3.3, pp. 11–12 (stab, good representatives)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Item 019 says the stabiliser splits but gives no cardinality. (6.6.7) needs the explicit order, and the multinomial cancellation in (6.6.8) depends on it. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Counting cuspidal pairs by rank, stabiliser and multiplicity profile
items.statement: Let a ≥ 1. Fix a partition (j^{c_j}) ⊢ a, integers k_d^j ≥ 0 (d | j) with Σ_{d|j} k_d^j = c_j, and partitions (i^{b_{d,i}^j}) ⊢ k_d^j. The number of inertial equivalence classes of everywhere-unramified cuspidal pairs (P,π̃) of G_a with these data (item 091) is ∏_{j≥1}∏_{d|j} binom(D_j(d), B_{j,d}) · B_{j,d}!/∏_{i≥1} b_{d,i}^j!, where B_{j,d} = Σ_i b_{d,i}^j.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the counting step that turns (6.6.4) into (6.6.10). It appears only as 'the distinct-type multinomial count' in item 096's proof outline. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Vanishing of the degree-e cone sum on a proper Levi
items.statement: Let L ≅ GL_(m_1)×…×GL_(m_k) be a standard Levi of GL_n with k ≥ 2, let d = gcd(m_1,…,m_k) and e ∈ Z, and let 1̂^e_Q (Q ∈ P(L)) be the functions of Prop. 5.2.1. Then Σ_(Q∈P(L)) 1̂^e_Q(λ) vanishes identically on X_L^G unless (n/d) | e; in particular it vanishes when gcd(e,n) = 1. When (n/d) | e the sum is a single monomial with root-of-unity values; for example it is ≡ 1 for L = T ⊂ GL_2 with e = 0. Proof sketch: the κ-signed cone series of §5.2.1 sum to the generating function of the classes H ∈ a_(L,Z)/X_*(Z_G) with zero projection to a_L^G, namely H = (j/d)(m_1,…,m_k) for 0 ≤ j < d. Their total degree jn/d is ≡ 0 mod n/d, so the degree-e part is empty unless (n/d) | e. Numerically verified for 12 Levis of GL_2 to GL_6 and every e.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Appendix A, pp. 75–76, input to Lemme A.2 (supplement; not stated in the paper)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the missing step of Lemme A.2. Without it the lemma is false for gcd(e,n) > 1, and with it the coprime case is proved. Items 116 and 119 depend on it. Route: AutomorphicSpectralTheory.

items.name: Admissible-cone division by the Jacobian factor
items.statement: For S ⊆ {1,…,g} let φ_S(t^m z^u) = m + Σ_(i∈S) u_i, and for a nonzero Laurent polynomial F ∈ Q[t^{±1},z_1^{±1},…,z_g^{±1}] let ord_S(F) be the minimum of φ_S over the monomials of F. Then ord_S(FG) = ord_S(F) + ord_S(G) and ord_S(J_g) = 0, where J_g = Π_i(1−z_i)(1−t/z_i). Since m + Σ_i min(u_i,0) = min_S φ_S(t^m z^u), it follows that if every monomial of F·J_g satisfies m + Σ min(u_i,0) ≥ 0, then so does every monomial of F.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.3, p. 74, Lemme 7.3.1 (proof) and the existence of Q_(g,n) (supplement repairing the printed argument)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): This is the correct form of the paper's 'plus petite valeur' argument, which is incomplete because m + Σ min(u_i,0) is not additive. Items 110 and 112 use it twice. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Gauss's lemma for multivariate Laurent polynomials
items.statement: Let R be a UFD with fraction field K, and let J ∈ R[z_1^{±1},…,z_g^{±1}] be primitive, i.e. the gcd of its coefficients is 1. If H ∈ R[z^{±1}] and H = I·J with I ∈ K[z^{±1}], then I ∈ R[z^{±1}]. Applications: R = Z[q], where J_g(q,1,z) is primitive because its coefficient at z_1⋯z_g is (−1)^g; and R = Q[q^{±1},z^{±1}] with J_g = Π(z−z_i)(1−q/z_i), which rules out a pole at z = 1.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.3, p. 74, Lemme 7.3.1 proof (supplement; the univariate case is mathlib:Polynomial.IsPrimitive.dvd_of_fraction_map_dvd_fraction_map, RingTheory/Polynomial/GaussLemma.lean:299)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Integral division by J_g needs Gauss's lemma for Laurent polynomials in several variables, over Z[q] and over Q[q^{±1},z^{±1}]. Mathlib has only the univariate version. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: Top-weight term of the bundle polynomial
items.statement: For g ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, with deg t = 2 and deg z_i = 1, A_(g,n) has degree 2((g−1)n²+1), and its unique monomial of that degree is t^{(g−1)n²+1}, with coefficient 1. Proof route for coprime e: q^{(g−1)n²+1}A_(g,n)(q,σ) = |Higgs^st_(n,e)(F_q)|, a smooth geometrically connected scheme of dimension D = 2(g−1)n²+2 (items 036 and 037; connectedness must be imported). By Deligne's weights, H^i_c has weights ≤ i < 2D except H^{2D}_c = Q_ℓ(−D). Pass from values to coefficients with a curve whose Weil numbers are multiplicatively independent (item 121). Alternatively, read the leading term off Mellit's formula. Verified for g = 1, 2, 3 and n ≤ 3 (n ≤ 4 for g = 2).
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §1, p. 3, Théorème 1.1(1) (input needed by its last sentence; supplement)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): Item 109 needs the leading term of the bundle polynomial, and no item supplies it; item 046 records only the cone condition. Route: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglandsCountingPartII.

items.name: p-free factorial factorisation of binomial coefficients
items.statement: Let p be prime and f_p as in item 104. For integers n ≥ m ≥ 0, binom(np,mp) = binom(n,m)·f_p(np)/(f_p(mp)f_p((n−m)p)). For n ≥ 1 and m ≥ 0, binom(−np,mp) = (−1)^{m(p−1)}·binom(−n,m)·f_p(np+mp)/(f_p(mp)f_p(np)). Proof: (Np)! = p^N N! f_p(Np), and binom(−N,M) = (−1)^M binom(N+M−1,M). Checked for p ≤ 5 and n < 8.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.2, p. 71 (displayed identities before the two cases)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-YU-23 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Théorème 7.2.3 uses these identities on p. 71–72 with no item; the sign (−1)^{m(p−1)} matters in the p = 2 case. Route: ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.

routes.reason: Yu supplies the unramified function-field specialization, exact degree/Haar conventions and the degree-zero spherical nonvanishing test inside existing arithmetic and automorphic layers. Import the pinned divisor results; do not duplicate the upstream curve/function-field dictionary.
Reuse the global bundle and full GL_n correspondence owners. The shifted HN and adelic orbit-mass interfaces are source additions inside GS.0, not a second shtuka or Langlands programme.

The existing spectral programme owns truncation, induced sections, residual spectrum, regularized families and the trace formula. Yu adds explicit finite-field degree lattices, finite torus fibres, spherical scalar normalizations and degree-cutoff formulas. Keep these as source contributions, including the corrected Lafforgue formula. The finite-cover transfer and smooth Fourier adapters145–150 are reusable AS.0 inputs;151–152 specialize AS.6, and153 specializes AS.1/2. Import142–144 from pinned Mathlib. These are function-field source additions to the programme, not an assertion that its number-field trace theorem already applies in characteristic p.

Whittaker normalization and unramified Rankin–Selberg product, pole and functional-equation calculations belong to the existing Rankin–Selberg layer. Import Langlands and cohomological weights/duality, preserving residual-segment and inertial-equivalence hypotheses.

The curve Weil-eigenvalue and pure lisse-coefficient input is already planned here. The Euler determinant formula and duality are imports from WeilConjectures:WC.1 and EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2:pairings, not new weight theorems.

Reuse the Hitchin/Higgs carrier already in the geometric fundamental-lemma layer. Its good-characteristic and sufficiently positive setup is not the all-characteristic coprime stable GL_n moduli theorem; item036 remains an additional endpoint in the counting extension. No reviewed ET.2b audit entry was found.

Formal coefficientwise series, partition cycle indices, plethystic operations and generalized-binomial coefficient manipulations belong in the existing formal q-series layer. Export them over general characteristic-zero coefficient rings and integral subrings, without introducing analytic convergence assumptions.

The binomial divisibility and p-free factorial congruences support arithmetic generating functions already in CA.2. Reuse existing binomial arithmetic; the exact Luo–Zhu congruence and its exceptional 2-adic case are the added source lemmas.

Import coherent Serre duality through SF.3 and its upstream JacobianChallenge Layer B supplier. The function-field Riemann–Roch theorem does not establish duality for arbitrary vector bundles on the scheme. No new Serre-duality programme is proposed.
The tensor H0/H2 calculation is an application of the existing smooth-proper perfect-pairing interface, with corrected Hom directions and Frobenius conventions.

The nonarchimedean negative-power-sum obstruction is a companion specialization of the existing independent finite-spectrum lemma. Reuse the pinned Vandermonde determinant instead of proposing a new exponential-sum owner.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: Counting unramified local systems
routes.reason: The existing GS programme constructs bundles, shtukas and Langlands, but not Yu's exact Frobenius-fixed counts, recurrence, integral universal polynomial, Jacobian quotient or degree independence. These require new counting layers after the existing correspondence, not a replacement correspondence.
routes.brief:
Final targets are Yu Theorem1.1: for g≥2 and n≥1 the Frobenius-fixed irreducible rank-n geometric local-system count is P_g,n(q^k,sigma_1^k,...,sigma_g^k), for a unique P_g,n in R_g=Z[z_i,t/z_i]^W. Its unique top-weight term is t^((g−1)n²+1); P_g,n=J_g Q_g,n with J_g=product_i(1−z_i)(1−t/z_i), Q_g,n in R_g and Q_g,n(1)=sum_(d|n)mu(d)mu(n/d)d^(2g−3). Prove Theorem1.3 J_e=P_n^e and Theorem1.4 dependence only on the order of e modulo n, the coprime Higgs comparison, and AppendixC's necessary exponent cone in every characteristic. Build, in order: Weil descent and twist stabilizers; isocline bundles and the geometric trace; the coprime stable GL_n coarse-moduli/mass adapter; finite spectral character sums; one reusable weighted matrix-tree/cofactor module and its cycle-block specialization; cuspidal orbit inversion and the exact recurrence097; universal Laurent polynomials and integral/Jacobian/Euler consequences. Import Function-field arithmetic (FunctionFieldArithmetic), Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields (GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands), Automorphic spectral theory (AutomorphicSpectralTheory), Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors), Deligne weights and purity (DeligneWeightsAndPurity), Etale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves), Q-series, partitions and mock modular forms (QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms), Classical arithmetic completion (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion), and the scheme curve suppliers through SchemeAndStackFoundations. Reuse Hitchin carriers from EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.2b, coordinate with the GWZ20-B endoscopic Part II, and consume ClassicalGroupsPartII's GSp character interpretation as optional explanatory infrastructure, not as a circular premise for polynomial integrality. Use Mathlib partition/graph/matrix/Mobius/Vandermonde primitives and Tau Ceti divisor/split-K0 results. Do not rebuild any upstream roadmap. Resolve S1–S8, especially exact spectral operators and external Higgs/monodromy proofs, before claiming the design has no gaps.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-YU-23), to respect when stating the layers:
- Lemme A.2 is false when gcd(e, n) > 1 (for n = 2, e = 0, c_Q ≡ 1 and μ₀ = (i, −i) the limit is 1). Add gcd(e, n) = 1. Yu's own proof of Théorème A.4, and so of Théorème 1.4, then covers only e prime to n; the general case of Théorème 1.4 is Mellit's theorem and must be imported, not derived from Appendix A. Théorèmes 1.1–1.3 use only coprime e and are unaffected.
- The top-weight assertion of Théorème 1.1(1) (leading term t^{(g−1)n²+1}) is stated but never proved. Prove it (new item) from the Higgs moduli dimension and the rank induction of (7.2.2).
- Lemme 7.3.1's last assertion needs g ≥ 2, and its cone argument must use the S-linear functionals φ_S (the printed functional is only superadditive). Théorème 7.2.3 needs the reduction for negative or zero S_i.
- In (5.3.2) (Proposition 5.3.4) the normalising factor pairs each root with L(Π_i × Π_j^∨), not L(Π_j × Π_i^∨). Proposition 5.1.1 is unaffected.
- Théorème 3.3.1 holds on lattice points T, not for real T, which is all the proof uses.
- The extraction's derivation items 142–153 and repairs 012, 032, 045, 046, 079, 083, 084, 110, 118 and 129 were checked and are sound; item 116's repair is sound only for gcd(e, n) = 1.

routes.title: Finite-dimensional representations of the classical groups, Part II: Rational symplectic-similitude characters
routes.reason: Yu's Remark7.1.1 needs rational algebraic GSp over Q and the tensor-generated integral character subring; the upstream classical-group roadmap treats classical highest weights and characters, mostly over C, and is imported rather than replanned.
routes.brief: Prove that restriction of rational algebraic representations of the split group GSp_2g to its diagonal torus identifies the representation ring with Z[t±1,z_i±1]^(S_g⋉(S2)^g), where a reciprocal swap sends z_i to t/z_i. Identify the tensor-generated subring of the standard representation with Z[z_i,t/z_i]^W, generated by t and the fundamental exterior expressions ∧^k V−t∧^(k−2)V, 1≤k≤g, with negative exterior degree interpreted as zero. Import Finite-dimensional representations of the classical groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/ClassicalGroups), especially Layers0,3,4, its reductive-group and highest-weight suppliers, and the existing TauCeti.SplitK0/TauCeti.repRing infrastructure. Supply the central-similitude weight lattice, rational-versus-complex base-change/descent, the correct algebraic representation category, character restriction/injectivity, and the integral tensor-generation argument. Do not apply the finite-group repRingCharacter_injective theorem to GSp(Q), or construct a second split Grothendieck ring. Accept rank-one GSp2=GL2, standard exterior-square multiplier and reciprocal-swap invariance as tests. The counting extension imports this interpretation without depending on it for its elementary cone definition.

review.reason: Checked on the page images of p. 9 and p. 18 and in the TeX. P(B) contains G: it indexes the sum (3.2.1), whose P = G term k_G is needed. For P = G, N_G = 1, so the p. 9 condition says ϕ(g) = 0 for all g and would kill every cusp form, including all of GL_1. For P = G, Δ̂_G = ∅, so τ̂_G ≡ 1 and the p. 18 condition fails for every g. sourceIssues.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §3.3.1, p. 18, Théorème 3.3.1, and its use on p. 20
sourceIssues.printed: En tant que fonction en T ∈ 𝔞_B, l'application T ↦ J_e^T est quasi-polynomiale au sens de la définition [Ch15, Définition 4.5.3].
sourceIssues.correction: The restriction of T ↦ J^T_e to lattice points T ∈ Hom(X^*(B), Z) ≅ Z^n is a quasi-polynomial in the sense of [Ch15, Déf. 4.5.3]. The same applies on p. 20 to the right-hand side via [Ch15, Prop. 4.5.5]: the equality holds for all lattice T with T_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ T_n. T = 0 is a lattice point, so J_e = P_n^e(X_1) follows unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: In Yu 𝔞_B = Hom(X^*(B), R) is real (§3.1.1). Ch15 Déf 4.5.3 (author p. 25, image read) defines quasi-polynomials on 𝔞_B as Σ_{ν∈f} p_ν(T) q^{⟨ν,T⟩} with p_ν polynomials and ν ∈ (2πi/log q)X^*(B) ⊗ Q, so they are real-analytic in T. J^T_e depends on T only through the indicators τ̂_P(H_B(δx) − T) with H_B(δx) in a lattice, so it is locally constant off the hyperplanes ϖ(T) ∈ (1/n)Z. It is not constant: by (3.3.7), for d(T) ≥ max(0, 2g−2) it counts T-semistable bundles of degree e, and this number is unbounded as d(T) → ∞ (already for n = 2 via L_1 ⊕ L_2). A non-constant locally constant function on the open chamber cannot be real-analytic, so the statement is false for real T. The inconsistency is inherited from Ch15, whose Example 4.5.4 counts floor functions as quasi-polynomial and whose Prop. 4.5.5 is stated on a lattice. The proof of Théorème 3.2.4 compares the two sides only at deep lattice points and evaluates at T = 0, so no result is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.3, p. 74: proof of Lemme 7.3.1 (cone condition for I_(g,n)) and the existence of Q_(g,n) ('par récurrence, le lemme précédent et le lemme de Gauss')
sourceIssues.printed: 'S'il y avait un monôme dans I_(g,n)(q,1,z_1,…,z_g) qui ne satisfaisait pas cette condition, on obtiendrait une contradiction en regardant les monômes q^m z^n apparaissant dans le produit de I_(g,n)(q,1,z) et J_g(q,1,z) tels que m + Σ min{n_i,0} prenne la plus petite valeur.'

With the S-linear functionals, a minimal monomial of I with S = {i : u_i < 0} survives in I·J. The conclusion is true: the cone condition was confirmed for I_(g,n) and Q_(g,n) for g ≤ 3.
